questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a concave mirror to form a real diminished image, the object must be placed

options.B: Between the mirror and its focus
options.C: Between the focus and the centre of curvature
options.E: At a distance greater than the radius of curvature

questions.ai_explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The unit of quantity of electricity (electric charge) is called
questions.ai_explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The resistance of a wire depends on
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.
questions.explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 2 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarities. What current flows through an external 1 Ω resistor?
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.
questions.explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which component is NOT contained in a zinc-carbon dry cell?
questions.ai_explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.
questions.explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
questions.ai_explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.
questions.explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: All heat generated in a 5 Ω resistor by a 2 A current flowing for 30 seconds evaporates 5 g of liquid at its boiling point. What is the specific latent heat of the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.
questions.explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a standing wave occurs in an air column, the distance between a node and its nearest antinode is equal to
questions.ai_explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.
questions.explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements are NOT correct? I. At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not affect the speed of sound in air treated as an ideal gas. II. The speed of sound in air increases with temperature. III. The quality of a note depends only on its frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.
questions.explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two identical tuning forks have natural frequency 256 Hz. One is loaded, and 4 beats per second are heard when they sound together. What is the frequency of the loaded fork?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.
questions.explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Dew point is the temperature at which water vapour in the atmosphere

options.D: Is just sufficient to cause cooling
options.E: Has a relative humidity of fifty percent

questions.ai_explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.
questions.explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The lower (0 °C) and upper (100 °C) fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. In a room, the mercury ends 49 mm above the lower point. What is the room temperature to one decimal place?
questions.ai_explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a solid changes directly into a gas when heat is applied the process is called
questions.ai_explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Heat is supplied at 100 W to 1.0 × 10⁻² kg of liquid for 20 seconds. Its temperature rises by 5 °C. Assuming the supplied heat warms the liquid, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).
questions.explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a model atmosphere, sea-level pressure is 10⁵ N/m², density is uniform at 1 kg/m³, and g = 10 m/s². What is the height of this atmosphere?
questions.ai_explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.
questions.explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the inertia of a body?

options.A: Ability to overcome the earth’s gravity
options.D: Reluctance to start moving and its readiness to stop moving once it has begun to move
options.E: Reluctance to start moving and its reluctance to stop moving once it has begun to move.

questions.ai_explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.
questions.explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A water pump at Kainji Dam lifts 1000 kg of water through a vertical height of 10 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its useful lifting power?
questions.ai_explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.
questions.explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What is the apparent colour of a RED SHIRT when viewed in PURE green light?
questions.ai_explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.
questions.explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which list gives the colours of the visible spectrum in order from longest to shortest wavelength?

options.A: Blue, red, green. Yellow, indigo, violet, orange.

questions.question: If a car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 10m s-2 for ten seconds, the distance it covers in the last one second of the motion is

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a force?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two masses 40g and 60g respectively, are attached firmly to the ends of a light metre rule. The centre of gravity of the system is

options.E: indeterminate because the metre-rule is light.

questions.explanation: Measure x from the 40 g mass. The centre of mass is x = (40 × 0 + 60 × 100)/(40 + 60) = 60 cm. It is therefore 40 cm from the heavier mass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two divers G and H are 20 m and 40 m below a lake surface. Their absolute pressures are P₁ and P₂ respectively. Atmospheric pressure equals 10 m of water. Find P₂/P₁ to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Absolute pressure includes atmospheric pressure. Thus P₁ = ρg(10 + 20) and P₂ = ρg(10 + 40). Their ratio is 50/30 = 1.67 to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Absolute pressure includes atmospheric pressure. Thus P₁ = ρg(10 + 20) and P₂ = ρg(10 + 40). Their ratio is 50/30 = 1.67 to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The areas of the effort and load pistons of a hydraulic press are 0.5m2 and 5m2 respectively. If a force F1 of 100N is applied on the effort piston, the force F2 on the load is
questions.ai_explanation: Pascal’s principle gives equal pressure in the two pistons: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂. Therefore F₂ = 100 × 5/0.5 = 1000 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Equal masses of liquids P at 20 °C and Q at 80 °C have specific heat capacities 1.0 and 1.5 J/(kg·°C), respectively. They are mixed in a lagged calorimeter. Neglect heat loss and the calorimeter’s heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: Heat lost by Q equals heat gained by P: 1.5(80 − T) = 1.0(T − 20). Hence 140 = 2.5T, giving T = 56 °C. Equal masses cancel from the equation.
questions.explanation: Heat lost by Q equals heat gained by P: 1.5(80 − T) = 1.0(T − 20). Hence 140 = 2.5T, giving T = 56 °C. Equal masses cancel from the equation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a gas experiment, the pressure of the gas is plotted against the reciprocal of the volume of the gas at a constant temperature. The unit of the slope of the resulting curve is
questions.ai_explanation: Slope is pressure divided by reciprocal volume, so its units are pressure × volume: (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. These are the units of work.
questions.explanation: Slope is pressure divided by reciprocal volume, so its units are pressure × volume: (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. These are the units of work.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Water shows anomalous behaviour
questions.ai_explanation: Between 0 °C and 4 °C, water contracts as it warms and expands as it cools. Its density is greatest at about 4 °C. This reversal of ordinary thermal expansion is its anomalous behaviour.
questions.explanation: Between 0 °C and 4 °C, water contracts as it warms and expands as it cools. Its density is greatest at about 4 °C. This reversal of ordinary thermal expansion is its anomalous behaviour.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement about a pure liquid in equilibrium with its vapour is NOT correct?

options.A: Boiling occurs when its saturated vapour pressure equals the external pressure.
options.B: Both its boiling point and its saturated vapour pressure at a fixed temperature depend on external pressure.
options.C: Its saturated vapour pressure rises as temperature increases.
options.D: Its saturated vapour pressure is independent of available volume while both liquid and vapour remain present.
options.E: Water can boil below 100 °C at high altitude.

questions.ai_explanation: At a fixed temperature, a pure liquid’s saturated vapour pressure is determined by the liquid and its temperature. External pressure sets the boiling temperature by the condition that vapour pressure equals external pressure.
questions.explanation: At a fixed temperature, a pure liquid’s saturated vapour pressure is determined by the liquid and its temperature. External pressure sets the boiling temperature by the condition that vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which phenomenon cannot be explained by a simple kinetic molecular model of matter alone?
questions.ai_explanation: Radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum. A simple kinetic molecular model alone does not describe this mechanism; electromagnetic theory is also needed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In order to find the depth of the sea. A ship sends out a sound wave and receives an echo after one second. If the velocity of sound in water is 1500m/s, what is the depth of the sea?
questions.ai_explanation: The echo time includes travel down to the seabed and back. Depth = vt/2 = 1500 × 1/2 = 750 m = 0.75 km.
questions.explanation: The echo time includes travel down to the seabed and back. Depth = vt/2 = 1500 × 1/2 = 750 m = 0.75 km.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a sound wave passes from air into water its

options.A: Speed and frequency increase but its wavelength remains the same.
options.B: Speed and wavelength increase but its frequency remains the same
options.D: Speed remains the same but its frequency and wavelength change.
options.E: Speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decrease.

questions.ai_explanation: Sound travels faster in water than in air. Its frequency stays fixed by the source as it crosses the boundary. Since λ = v/f, the wavelength increases with speed.
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in water than in air. Its frequency stays fixed by the source as it crosses the boundary. Since λ = v/f, the wavelength increases with speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe organ on a day when the speed of sound is 340m s-1 is 170 Hz, then the length of the pipe is
questions.ai_explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, L = λ/4 = v/(4f). Thus L = 340/(4 × 170) = 0.50 m = 50 cm, neglecting end correction.
questions.explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, L = λ/4 = v/(4f). Thus L = 340/(4 × 170) = 0.50 m = 50 cm, neglecting end correction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed 15cm in front of a concave mirror of radius 40cm. The image formed is

options.B: Real and 60cm in front of the mirror

questions.ai_explanation: The focal length is R/2 = 20 cm. With real distances positive, 1/v = 1/20 − 1/15 = −1/60. Thus the image is virtual, 60 cm behind the mirror; the object lies inside the focus.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 45° triangular glass prism can be used as a reflector of light because

options.A: Refraction never takes place in such a prism
options.B: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence
options.C: The refractive index of glass is less than 1
options.E: The critical angle for glass is less than 45°

questions.ai_explanation: In a right-angled 45° glass prism, a ray entering normally at a short face reaches the long face at 45°. If the glass–air critical angle is smaller, total internal reflection occurs there.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two rays from a point under a flat water surface lie in the same vertical plane, symmetrically about the vertical. Their angle in water is 60°. Find their angle in air to one decimal place. Take the refractive index of water as 4/3.
questions.ai_explanation: Each ray is 30° from the normal in water. Snell’s law gives sin r = (4/3)sin 30° = 2/3, so r = 41.81°. The emergent rays are separated by 2r = 83.6° to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Each ray is 30° from the normal in water. Snell’s law gives sin r = (4/3)sin 30° = 2/3, so r = 41.81°. The emergent rays are separated by 2r = 83.6° to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following will convert a milliammeter to a voltmeter?

options.E: Parallel resistance equal to milliameter resistance.

questions.ai_explanation: A high resistance in series limits the current through the meter. The resulting combination measures a larger voltage because V = I(Rseries + Rmeter).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An electric kettle connected to 240 V produces 6.0 × 10⁵ J of heat in 5 minutes. Find its resistance.
questions.ai_explanation: Five minutes is 300 s. Power = E/t = 600000/300 = 2000 W. Using P = V²/R gives R = 240²/2000 = 28.8 Ω.
questions.explanation: Five minutes is 300 s. Power = E/t = 600000/300 = 2000 W. Using P = V²/R gives R = 240²/2000 = 28.8 Ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: On which of the following does the operation of a moving coil ammeter depend? I Electromagnetic induction. II Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. III Magnetic effect of an electric current.
questions.ai_explanation: A current-carrying coil experiences magnetic forces that produce a turning effect in the meter’s magnetic field. These are the magnetic effect of current and the force on a current-carrying conductor, so II and III apply.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about electrolysis is NOT correct?

options.A: The substances in solution in the electrolyte become ionized.

questions.ai_explanation: Faraday’s law gives deposited mass m = MIt/(nF). For the same material and duration, mass is proportional to current, not to its square.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which unit is equivalent to kg·m·s⁻¹?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two objects, one with three times the mass of the other, are dropped together from the same height. Neglect air resistance. While falling above the ground, they have the same

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a box of mass 400g is given an initial speed of 5m s-1, it slides along a horizontal floor a distance of 3m before coming to rest. What is the coefficient of the kinetic friction between the box and the floor? (g = 10m s-2)
questions.ai_explanation: Work done against friction equals the initial kinetic energy: μmg × 3 = ½m × 5². Cancelling mass gives μ = 25/(2 × 10 × 3) = 5/12.

questions.question: A 1000 kg elevator descends with a downward acceleration of 1.0 m/s². If g = 10.0 m/s², what is the tension in its suspending cable?

questions.question: Thermal expansion of solids can be a disadvantage in the

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Calculate the heat required to convert 2 kg of ice at −2 °C to water at 0 °C. The specific heat capacity of ice is 2090 J/(kg·°C), and its specific latent heat of fusion is 333 kJ/kg.

questions.explanation: First warm the ice by 2 °C: Q₁ = 2 × 2090 × 2 = 8360 J. Then melt it: Q₂ = 2 × 333000 = 666000 J. Total heat is 674360 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In which of the following are the substances arranged in descending order of their thermal conductivities?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The vacuum in the Thermos flask helps to reduce heat transfer by

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Why is a house with a white-painted roof generally cooler in hot sunshine than an otherwise similar house with a black-painted roof?

questions.explanation: A white coating generally reflects more incoming sunlight than a black coating. With less solar energy absorbed, the roof gains less heat under otherwise similar conditions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to produce a nearly pure tone?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed between two plane mirrors inclined at 90°. How many images are formed?

questions.explanation: Two plane mirrors at right angles form one image by reflection in each mirror and a third by successive reflections in both. Thus there are three images.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object 3.0cm high is placed 60.0cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0cm. Calculate the size of the image formed.
questions.ai_explanation: The lens formula gives 1/v = 1/20 − 1/60 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. Magnification magnitude is v/u = 30/60 = 0.5. Image height is 0.5 × 3.0 = 1.5 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Four lenses are being considered for use as a microscope objective. Which of the following focal lengths is most suitable?

questions.explanation: A microscope objective uses a converging lens with a short focal length. Positive 5 mm provides stronger convergence than positive 5 cm, making it the suitable choice here.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At a place with magnetic declination 10°E, a compass reads N40°E. What is the true geographic bearing?
questions.ai_explanation: Magnetic north is 10° east of true north. A compass direction 40° east of magnetic north is therefore 10° + 40° = 50° east of true north: N50°E.
questions.explanation: Magnetic north is 10° east of true north. A compass direction 40° east of magnetic north is therefore 10° + 40° = 50° east of true north: N50°E.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Capacitors of 6 μF and 8 μF are in series. What additional capacitor, connected in series with them, gives a total capacitance of 3 μF?
questions.ai_explanation: For series capacitors, reciprocals add: 1/3 = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/C. Thus 1/C = 1/24 and the additional capacitance is 24 μF.
questions.explanation: For series capacitors, reciprocals add: 1/3 = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/C. Thus 1/C = 1/24 and the additional capacitance is 24 μF.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An ideal transformer operating with a load has more turns on its secondary than its primary. It

options.A: Has a smaller secondary current than primary current
options.B: Has greater output power than input power
options.D: Increases the total energy output above its input

questions.ai_explanation: An ideal transformer with more secondary turns steps voltage up. Conservation of power gives VsIs = VpIp, so the secondary current is smaller than the primary current.
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer with more secondary turns steps voltage up. Conservation of power gives VsIs = VpIp, so the secondary current is smaller than the primary current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field at a point in the vicinity of a bar magnet is

options.A: Always towards the north pole of the magnet
options.B: Always away from the south pole of the magnet
options.C: Along the line joining the point to the neutral point
options.D: In the direction the north pole of a compass needle would point.

questions.ai_explanation: The direction of a magnetic field is defined as the direction in which the north-seeking pole of a small compass points at that location.
questions.explanation: The direction of a magnetic field is defined as the direction in which the north-seeking pole of a small compass points at that location.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When two parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions, the force on either wire is

options.B: Zero, because the currents cancel each other
options.C: Twice as much as when the currents are in the same direction

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is true of the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect?

options.B: The maximum emitted-electron energy is independent of the surface work function
options.C: The maximum emitted-electron energy depends on the incident wavelength
options.D: At fixed wavelength, greater light intensity necessarily gives greater maximum emitted-electron energy

questions.ai_explanation: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, maximum kinetic energy is Kmax = hc/λ − φ. It depends on wavelength and work function. Increasing intensity at fixed wavelength chiefly increases the number emitted.
questions.explanation: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, maximum kinetic energy is Kmax = hc/λ − φ. It depends on wavelength and work function. Increasing intensity at fixed wavelength chiefly increases the number emitted.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Isotopes are nuclei which have

options.A: The same number of neutrons and electrons
options.B: Equal number of electrons and protons
options.C: The same atomic number but different number of neutrons
options.D: The same number of total particles.

questions.ai_explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number, meaning the same number of protons, but different neutron numbers. Their mass numbers therefore differ.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number, meaning the same number of protons, but different neutron numbers. Their mass numbers therefore differ.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a set of vectors?

options.A: Force, mass and moment of force
options.B: Acceleration, velocity and moment of force

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which SI units are correctly matched? I. N for force. II. N·m⁻¹ for torque. III. W for power. IV. kg·m·s⁻² for momentum.
questions.ai_explanation: Force is measured in newtons and power in watts, so I and III are correct. Torque is measured in N·m, not N/m. Momentum is kg·m/s, not kg·m/s².
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons and power in watts, so I and III are correct. Torque is measured in N·m, not N/m. Momentum is kg·m/s, not kg·m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The magnitude of the resultant of two mutually perpendicular forces, F1 and F2 is 13N. If the magnitude of F1 is 5N, what is the magnitude of F2?
questions.ai_explanation: Perpendicular forces obey R² = F₁² + F₂². Therefore F₂ = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 N.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular forces obey R² = F₁² + F₂². Therefore F₂ = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A velocity–time graph contains points (5 s, 10 m/s) and (20 s, 20 m/s). Find the mean acceleration between them to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Mean acceleration is change in velocity divided by elapsed time: (20 − 10)/(20 − 5) = 10/15 = 0.67 m/s² to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Mean acceleration is change in velocity divided by elapsed time: (20 − 10)/(20 − 5) = 10/15 = 0.67 m/s² to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two perpendicular forces have resultant 100 N. One force makes 30° with the resultant. Find that force’s magnitude to one decimal place.
questions.ai_explanation: The force making 30° with the resultant is the adjacent component: F = R cos 30° = 100 × √3/2 = 86.6 N to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The force making 30° with the resultant is the adjacent component: F = R cos 30° = 100 × √3/2 = 86.6 N to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities are scalars? I Electrical potential II Torque III Momentum IV Kinetic energy
questions.ai_explanation: Electric potential and kinetic energy are scalars. Torque and momentum are vectors, so the scalar quantities are I and IV.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A footballer applies an average force of 30.0 N to a stationary ball for 0.05 s. If the ball’s mass is 0.075 kg, what is its speed as it moves off?
questions.ai_explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. Starting from rest, mv = Ft = 30.0 × 0.05 = 1.5 N·s. Hence v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s.
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. Starting from rest, mv = Ft = 30.0 × 0.05 = 1.5 N·s. Hence v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20-tooth gear drives a 60-tooth gear. If the smaller gear rotates at 120 rev/s, what is the angular speed of the larger gear?
questions.ai_explanation: Meshing gears pass the same number of teeth per second. Therefore 20 × 120 = 60 × n, giving the larger gear’s speed n = 40 rev/s.
questions.explanation: Meshing gears pass the same number of teeth per second. Therefore 20 × 120 = 60 × n, giving the larger gear’s speed n = 40 rev/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 60 kg man climbs through a vertical height of 22 m with useful lifting power 0.25 kW. How long does the climb take? Use g = 10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: Useful energy for the climb is mgh = 60 × 10 × 22 = 13200 J. At 0.25 kW = 250 W, time = energy/power = 13200/250 = 52.8 s.
questions.explanation: Useful energy for the climb is mgh = 60 × 10 × 22 = 13200 J. At 0.25 kW = 250 W, time = energy/power = 13200/250 = 52.8 s.

questions.question: The product PV where P is pressure and V is volume has the same unit as

questions.explanation: Pressure × volume has units (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. A joule is the SI unit of energy.

questions.question: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 10kg of copper by1K is its

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following media allow the transmission of sound waves through them? I Air II Liquids III Solids

questions.question: Which behaviours can both mechanical and electromagnetic waves exhibit under suitable conditions? I. Diffraction. II. Refraction. III. Interference.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the usual nondispersive ideal-gas model for air of fixed composition, which factor independently affects sound speed? I. Temperature. II. Pressure at fixed temperature. III. Frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: For air treated as an ideal gas, sound speed is √(γRT/M). At fixed composition it depends on temperature. Pressure has no independent effect at fixed temperature, and frequency does not enter this model.
questions.explanation: For air treated as an ideal gas, sound speed is √(γRT/M). At fixed composition it depends on temperature. Pressure has no independent effect at fixed temperature, and frequency does not enter this model.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of sound in air at sea-level is 340m s-1 while that of light is 300,000km s-1. How far (to the nearest metre) from the center of thunderstorm is an observer who hears a thunder 2s after a lightning flash?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two uniform strings of equal length and equal tension sound their fundamental notes in frequency ratio 4:1. What is their corresponding mass ratio?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Connecting a resistance R across a cell reduces its terminal voltage to two-thirds of its open-circuit emf. What is the cell’s internal resistance?

questions.explanation: An induction coil uses a changing current to change magnetic flux through another winding. Faraday’s law relates that changing flux to the induced emf.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the kinetic theory of an ideal gas, absolute temperature is a

options.D: Physical property proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of its molecules

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a sound wave in air, the adjacent rarefactions and compressions are separated by a distance of 17cm. If the velocity of the sound wave is 340ms-1, determine the frequency.

questions.question: Light of free-space wavelength 5000 × 10⁻⁸ cm enters glass of refractive index 1.5. Find its wavelength in glass, rounding the coefficient of 10⁻⁸ cm to the nearest integer.

questions.explanation: Frequency stays unchanged on entering glass, while speed becomes c/n. Therefore wavelength becomes λ/n = (5000/1.5) × 10⁻⁸ cm ≈ 3333 × 10⁻⁸ cm.
