questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What liquid-column height supports atmospheric pressure 102000 N/m² if liquid density is 2600 kg/m³ and g = 10 m/s²? Give the answer to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrostatic pressure is p = ρgh. Thus h = 102000/(2600 × 10) = 3.923… m, or 3.92 m to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure is p = ρgh. Thus h = 102000/(2600 × 10) = 3.923… m, or 3.92 m to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A platinum wire has resistance 0.75 Ω at 0 °C and 1.05 Ω at 100 °C. Assuming linear variation, find its temperature when resistance is 0.90 Ω.
questions.ai_explanation: The 0–100 °C resistance change is 1.05 − 0.75 = 0.30 Ω. The measured rise is 0.90 − 0.75 = 0.15 Ω, half the interval. Temperature is therefore 50.0 °C.
questions.explanation: The 0–100 °C resistance change is 1.05 − 0.75 = 0.30 Ω. The measured rise is 0.90 − 0.75 = 0.15 Ω, half the interval. Temperature is therefore 50.0 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed amount of gas is cooled at constant volume without condensation. Its pressure decreases because its molecules

options.A: Collide less frequently with the walls of the container.
options.B: Have the same average kinetic energy

questions.ai_explanation: Cooling lowers the molecules’ average kinetic energy and speed. At fixed volume they strike the walls less often and with less momentum change per collision, reducing the gas pressure.
questions.explanation: Cooling lowers the molecules’ average kinetic energy and speed. At fixed volume they strike the walls less often and with less momentum change per collision, reducing the gas pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 1 kg copper block at 100 °C is placed on ice at 0 °C. Neglect heat loss. Find the mass melted to the nearest gram, using copper’s specific heat capacity 400 J/(kg·K) and ice’s latent heat of fusion 333 × 10³ J/kg.
questions.ai_explanation: The copper loses Q = mcΔT = 1 × 400 × 100 = 40000 J. This melts ice of mass Q/L = 40000/333000 = 0.12012… kg, or 120 g to the nearest gram.
questions.explanation: The copper loses Q = mcΔT = 1 × 400 × 100 = 40000 J. This melts ice of mass Q/L = 40000/333000 = 0.12012… kg, or 120 g to the nearest gram.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At external pressure 750 mmHg, what change is needed to make pure water boil at 100 °C?

options.C: Heat more rapidly at the same pressure
options.D: Reduce the external pressure by a quarter

questions.ai_explanation: Pure water boils near 100 °C at about 760 mmHg. At 750 mmHg it boils slightly below 100 °C. Raising the external pressure to about 760 mmHg raises the boiling point to 100 °C.
questions.explanation: Pure water boils near 100 °C at about 760 mmHg. At 750 mmHg it boils slightly below 100 °C. Raising the external pressure to about 760 mmHg raises the boiling point to 100 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In ordinary heat-transfer experiments, which statements are correct? I. Land and sea breezes are natural convection currents. II. Convection occurs in liquids or gases, rather than solids retaining their fixed shape. III. The vacuum gap in a thermos flask prevents heat transfer by convection only.
questions.ai_explanation: Land and sea breezes arise from natural convection. In ordinary heat-transfer experiments, convection is bulk motion of a liquid or gas. A vacuum suppresses both conduction and convection across the gap, so III is false.
questions.explanation: Land and sea breezes arise from natural convection. In ordinary heat-transfer experiments, convection is bulk motion of a liquid or gas. A vacuum suppresses both conduction and convection across the gap, so III is false.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Geometrical shadows and eclipses result primarily from the
questions.ai_explanation: In a uniform medium, light travels approximately in straight lines. An opaque object blocks those paths and produces a shadow; an eclipse occurs when a celestial body blocks the light reaching another body or observer.
questions.explanation: In a uniform medium, light travels approximately in straight lines. An opaque object blocks those paths and produces a shadow; an eclipse occurs when a celestial body blocks the light reaching another body or observer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object 3 cm high is placed vertically 10 cm in front of a concave mirror. Its image is 40 cm from the mirror. Find the magnitude of the image height.
questions.ai_explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What must be the distance between an object and a converging lens of focal length 20cm to produce an erect image two times the object height?
questions.ai_explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.
questions.explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In an uncorrected short-sighted eye, light rays from a point on a very distant object are focused

options.B: On the retina by a converging lens
options.C: Behind the retina by a diverging lens
options.D: In front of the retina a distance 2F from the lens.

questions.ai_explanation: In an uncorrected short-sighted eye, parallel rays from a distant object converge before reaching the retina. A diverging corrective lens reduces the eye system’s convergence so the focus moves back onto the retina.
questions.explanation: In an uncorrected short-sighted eye, parallel rays from a distant object converge before reaching the retina. A diverging corrective lens reduces the eye system’s convergence so the focus moves back onto the retina.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Under white illumination, which primary colour does an ideal magenta surface absorb?
questions.ai_explanation: An ideal magenta surface reflects red and blue light and absorbs green. Under white illumination, the reflected red and blue combine to appear magenta.
questions.explanation: An ideal magenta surface reflects red and blue light and absorbs green. Under white illumination, the reflected red and blue combine to appear magenta.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a resonance tube closed at one end, the first resonant air-column length is 20 cm for a 480 Hz tuning fork. Neglect end correction and find the speed of sound.
questions.ai_explanation: At the first resonance of a tube closed at one end, L = λ/4. Thus λ = 4 × 0.20 = 0.80 m and v = fλ = 480 × 0.80 = 384 m/s.
questions.explanation: At the first resonance of a tube closed at one end, L = λ/4. Thus λ = 4 × 0.20 = 0.80 m and v = fλ = 480 × 0.80 = 384 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An organ pipe closed at one end is 80 cm long. Neglect end correction. Find its fundamental frequency to the nearest hertz if sound speed is 340 m/s.
questions.ai_explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, λ = 4L = 3.20 m. Frequency is 340/3.20 = 106.25 Hz, or 106 Hz to the nearest hertz.
questions.explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, λ = 4L = 3.20 m. Frequency is 340/3.20 = 106.25 Hz, or 106 Hz to the nearest hertz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An insulated body is at rest in electrostatic equilibrium with positive net charge. Which statements are true? I. Positive charge exceeds negative charge. II. It creates an electric field. III. It stores electrostatic energy relative to its discharged state. IV. It carries a steady electric current.
questions.ai_explanation: Positive net charge means there is more positive than negative charge, usually through an electron deficit. The charged body creates a field and stores electrostatic energy. At rest in electrostatic equilibrium, it carries no steady current.
questions.explanation: Positive net charge means there is more positive than negative charge, usually through an electron deficit. The charged body creates a field and stores electrostatic energy. At rest in electrostatic equilibrium, it carries no steady current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a vector?
questions.ai_explanation: Electric field is force per unit positive test charge, so it has both magnitude and direction. Electric charge, potential difference and capacitance are scalars.
questions.explanation: Electric field is force per unit positive test charge, so it has both magnitude and direction. Electric charge, potential difference and capacitance are scalars.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three identical cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarity across a 2.67 Ω load. Find the load current to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V and have internal resistance 1/3 Ω. The load current is 1.5/(2.67 + 1/3) = 0.4994… A, or 0.50 A to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V and have internal resistance 1/3 Ω. The load current is 1.5/(2.67 + 1/3) = 0.4994… A, or 0.50 A to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a uniform metre bridge, a 2.0 Ω standard resistor occupies the gap beside the 0 cm end. The balance point is 55.0 cm from that end. Find the resistance in the other gap to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform metre bridge, resistance ratio equals wire-length ratio at balance. With 2.0 Ω beside the 0 cm end, 2.0/R = 55/45. Thus R = 2.0 × 45/55 = 1.64 Ω to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: For a uniform metre bridge, resistance ratio equals wire-length ratio at balance. With 2.0 Ω beside the 0 cm end, 2.0/R = 55/45. Thus R = 2.0 × 45/55 = 1.64 Ω to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The energy supplied by an electrical source per unit positive charge for a complete circuit is its
questions.ai_explanation: Emf is the energy supplied by a source per unit charge passing through it. That energy is transferred around the complete circuit, including the source’s internal resistance. Its unit is the volt, or joule per coulomb.
questions.explanation: Emf is the energy supplied by a source per unit charge passing through it. That energy is transferred around the complete circuit, including the source’s internal resistance. Its unit is the volt, or joule per coulomb.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is an essential physical property of the wires used for making fuses?
questions.ai_explanation: A fuse element must melt when excessive current heats it sufficiently. Melting opens the circuit and stops the sustained overcurrent. A suitably low melting point supports this protective action.
questions.explanation: A fuse element must melt when excessive current heats it sufficiently. Melting opens the circuit and stops the sustained overcurrent. A suitably low melting point supports this protective action.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For the same transmitted power, using a higher voltage reduces energy lost in the transmission wires through
questions.ai_explanation: For the same transmitted power, increasing voltage reduces current because P = VI. Heating loss in the wires is I²R, so lowering current reduces heat dissipation.
questions.explanation: For the same transmitted power, increasing voltage reduces current because P = VI. Heating loss in the wires is I²R, so lowering current reduces heat dissipation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer with full-scale current 10 mA and coil resistance 30 Ω is converted to a 10 A ammeter. Which approximate resistor and connection are required?
questions.ai_explanation: The full-scale coil voltage is 0.010 × 30 = 0.30 V. The shunt carries 10 − 0.010 = 9.99 A, so its resistance is 0.30/9.99 ≈ 0.03 Ω. It must be parallel to the coil.
questions.explanation: The full-scale coil voltage is 0.010 × 30 = 0.30 V. The shunt carries 10 − 0.010 = 9.99 A, so its resistance is 0.30/9.99 ≈ 0.03 Ω. It must be parallel to the coil.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What precaution should a manufacturer take to ensure that energy loss in a transformer is minimized?

options.A: Make the windings from high-resistance wire
options.B: Make the magnetic core from thin, electrically insulated metal sheets
options.C: Use no magnetic material in the core
options.D: Minimize flux linking the primary and secondary coils

questions.ai_explanation: A transformer core made from thin, electrically insulated metal laminations restricts large circulating eddy currents. This reduces unwanted heating in the core.
questions.explanation: A transformer core made from thin, electrically insulated metal laminations restricts large circulating eddy currents. This reduces unwanted heating in the core.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A photoemissive photocell works on the principle of

options.B: Emission of electrons by incident radiation
options.C: Emission of protons by incident electrons

questions.ai_explanation: A photoemissive cell uses incident photons to release electrons from a photosensitive surface. Those electrons can be collected to produce a measurable current.
questions.explanation: A photoemissive cell uses incident photons to release electrons from a photosensitive surface. Those electrons can be collected to produce a measurable current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object moves with uniform speed round a circle. Its acceleration has
questions.ai_explanation: Centripetal acceleration has magnitude v²/r. Both speed and radius are constant, so this magnitude stays constant. Its direction continually changes as it points from the moving object toward the centre.
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration has magnitude v²/r. Both speed and radius are constant, so this magnitude stays constant. Its direction continually changes as it points from the moving object toward the centre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20 kg load is pulled at constant speed along a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. If the plane’s efficiency is 75%, find the pulling force parallel to the plane to one decimal place. Use g = 10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: Efficiency is useful work divided by input work. For motion through distance s along the slope, 0.75 = mg(s sin 30°)/(Fs). Thus F = 20 × 10 × 0.5/0.75 = 133.3 N to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Efficiency is useful work divided by input work. For motion through distance s along the slope, 0.75 = mg(s sin 30°)/(Fs). Thus F = 20 × 10 × 0.5/0.75 = 133.3 N to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The spiral spring of a spring balance is 25.0cm long when 5N hangs on it and 30.0cm long, when the weight is 10N. What is the length of the spring if the weight is 3N assuming Hooke’s Law is obeyed?
questions.ai_explanation: An extra 5 N extends the spring by 5 cm, giving compliance 1 cm/N. Its unloaded length is 25 − 5 = 20 cm. With 3 N attached, its length is 20 + 3 = 23 cm.
questions.explanation: An extra 5 N extends the spring by 5 cm, giving compliance 1 cm/N. Its unloaded length is 25 − 5 = 20 cm. With 3 N attached, its length is 20 + 3 = 23 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stone gives an apparent mass reading of 15.0 g when fully immersed in water and 10.0 g when fully immersed in a liquid of relative density 2.0. Neglect air buoyancy. Find its mass in air.
questions.ai_explanation: Let b be the mass-equivalent buoyancy in water and m the true mass. Then m − b = 15 g and m − 2b = 10 g. Subtracting gives b = 5 g, so m = 20 g.
questions.explanation: Let b be the mass-equivalent buoyancy in water and m the true mass. Then m − b = 15 g and m − 2b = 10 g. Subtracting gives b = 5 g, so m = 20 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In which of the following is surface tension important?

options.A: The floating of a ship in water
options.B: The floating of a dry needle in water
options.C: The floating of a balloon in air
options.D: The diffusion of a sugar solution across membrane.

questions.ai_explanation: Surface tension can support a carefully placed dry needle at the water surface. A ship and a balloon are mainly supported by buoyancy, while membrane diffusion is driven by concentration differences.
questions.explanation: Surface tension can support a carefully placed dry needle at the water surface. A ship and a balloon are mainly supported by buoyancy, while membrane diffusion is driven by concentration differences.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At normal atmospheric pressure, how much more heat is released by 4 kg of steam at 100 °C than by 4 kg of water at 100 °C when each ends as water at 80 °C? Use latent heat 2260000 J/kg and water specific heat 4200 J/(kg·K).
questions.ai_explanation: Both samples release 4 × 4200 × 20 = 336000 J as water cools from 100 °C to 80 °C. The steam also releases 4 × 2260000 = 9040000 J on condensing. That latent heat is the difference.
questions.explanation: Both samples release 4 × 4200 × 20 = 336000 J as water cools from 100 °C to 80 °C. The steam also releases 4 × 2260000 = 9040000 J on condensing. That latent heat is the difference.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: How long does a 750 W heater take to raise 1 kg of water from 20 °C to 50 °C, neglecting heat losses? Use specific heat capacity 4200 J/(kg·K).
questions.ai_explanation: Required heat is mcΔT = 1 × 4200 × (50 − 20) = 126000 J. At 750 J/s, the heater needs 126000/750 = 168 s if no heat is lost.
questions.explanation: Required heat is mcΔT = 1 × 4200 × (50 − 20) = 126000 J. At 750 J/s, the heater needs 126000/750 = 168 s if no heat is lost.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a pure liquid in equilibrium with its vapour, the saturated vapour pressure increases as the

options.A: Volume of the liquid increases at fixed temperature
options.B: Volume of the liquid decreases at fixed temperature, with liquid still present

questions.ai_explanation: Saturated vapour pressure rises with temperature. Warmer liquid molecules have greater energy, and equilibrium is reached at a higher vapour pressure. At a fixed temperature it does not depend on the liquid amount while both phases remain.
questions.explanation: Saturated vapour pressure rises with temperature. Warmer liquid molecules have greater energy, and equilibrium is reached at a higher vapour pressure. At a fixed temperature it does not depend on the liquid amount while both phases remain.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The absolute temperature of a perfect gas is proportional to the average

options.C: Translational kinetic energy of the molecules

questions.ai_explanation: For an ideal gas, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3kT/2. It is therefore directly proportional to the absolute temperature T.
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3kT/2. It is therefore directly proportional to the absolute temperature T.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is true of light waves and sound waves in air?

options.B: They both need a material medium for propagation
options.D: Their speeds in air are equal

questions.ai_explanation: Both light and sound transfer energy. Light can travel through vacuum, while sound needs matter. In air, sound is longitudinal and much slower than light.
questions.explanation: Both light and sound transfer energy. Light can travel through vacuum, while sound needs matter. In air, sound is longitudinal and much slower than light.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The image in pin-hole camera is

options.A: Erect and formed by refraction through a lens
options.C: Erect and gets sharper as the hole becomes larger
options.D: Inverted and formed by the light from each point traveling in a straight line.

questions.ai_explanation: Rays from the top of an object pass through the small hole to the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom reach the top. Straight-line propagation therefore produces an inverted real image.
questions.explanation: Rays from the top of an object pass through the small hole to the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom reach the top. Straight-line propagation therefore produces an inverted real image.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A plane mirror is rotated through a small angle Q in the plane of incidence while the incident ray remains fixed. Through what angle does the reflected ray rotate?
questions.ai_explanation: With the incident ray fixed, rotating the mirror also rotates its normal by Q. The equal-angle reflection law makes the reflected direction change by twice that angle, or 2Q.
questions.explanation: With the incident ray fixed, rotating the mirror also rotates its normal by Q. The equal-angle reflection law makes the reflected direction change by twice that angle, or 2Q.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a ray diagram for a thin converging lens, a ray that is not parallel to the optic axis but passes through the optic center will

options.B: Pass through the center of curvature after refraction
options.C: Emerge parallel to the principal axis
options.D: Pass through the principal focus after refraction.

questions.ai_explanation: In the thin-lens approximation, a ray through the optical centre is treated as undeviated. The small lateral displacement through a real lens is neglected in the ray diagram.
questions.explanation: In the thin-lens approximation, a ray through the optical centre is treated as undeviated. The small lateral displacement through a real lens is neglected in the ray diagram.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the image of an object, 4cm from a diverging lens of focal length –12cm?

options.A: The image is virtual, 3cm in front of the lens
options.B: The image is real, 6cm behind the lens
options.C: The image is virtual, 6cm in front of the lens
options.D: The image is real, 3cm in front of the lens.

questions.ai_explanation: Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/12 − 1/4 = −1/3, so v = −3 cm. The negative image distance means a virtual image on the same side as the object.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/12 − 1/4 = −1/3, so v = −3 cm. The negative image distance means a virtual image on the same side as the object.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256Hz and 260 Hz are sounded close to each other. What is the frequency of the beats produced?
questions.ai_explanation: Beats arise from alternating reinforcement and cancellation of nearby frequencies. Their frequency is the absolute difference: |260 − 256| = 4 Hz.
questions.explanation: Beats arise from alternating reinforcement and cancellation of nearby frequencies. Their frequency is the absolute difference: |260 − 256| = 4 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about the earth’s magnetic field?

options.A: The angle of dip is the angle which a free suspended magnet makes with the vertical
options.B: The angle of declination is the angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian
options.C: The angle of declination is the angle which a magnetic compass makes with the magnetic meridian.
options.D: The angle of inclination is the difference between the angle of dip and the angle of declination.

questions.ai_explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between geographic north and magnetic north. Dip, or inclination, is instead the angle of the magnetic field relative to the horizontal.
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between geographic north and magnetic north. Dip, or inclination, is instead the angle of the magnetic field relative to the horizontal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The function of the system of granulated carbon mixed with manganese (IV) oxide in a Leclanche cell is to

options.A: Increase the emf of the cell to 2.0 V
options.B: Prevent local action in the cell
options.D: Make the cell black and hence a good radiator

questions.ai_explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide is reduced in the cell’s cathode reaction and serves as the depolarizer. Carbon improves electrical conduction in the mixture, helping the cell deliver current.
questions.explanation: Manganese(IV) oxide is reduced in the cell’s cathode reaction and serves as the depolarizer. Carbon improves electrical conduction in the mixture, helping the cell deliver current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A resistive device dissipates 1500 W and has resistance 375 Ω. What current does it draw?
questions.ai_explanation: For a resistive device, P = I²R. Hence I = √(P/R) = √(1500/375) = √4 = 2.00 A.
questions.explanation: For a resistive device, P = I²R. Hence I = √(P/R) = √(1500/375) = √4 = 2.00 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: To convert an alternating current dynamo into a direct current dynamo, the

options.A: Number of turns in the coil is increased
options.B: Strength of the field magnet is increased
options.C: Slip rings are replaced with a split-ring commutator
options.D: Coil is wound on a soft-iron armature

questions.ai_explanation: A split-ring commutator reverses the coil’s connection to the external circuit every half-turn. The external current then flows in one direction, giving pulsating direct current rather than alternating current.
questions.explanation: A split-ring commutator reverses the coil’s connection to the external circuit every half-turn. The external current then flows in one direction, giving pulsating direct current rather than alternating current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of platinum is 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ kg/C. How long must a 100 A current flow to deposit 1.0 kg of platinum, to one decimal place in hours?
questions.ai_explanation: Using m = ZIt, time is 1/(5.0 × 10⁻⁷ × 100) = 20000 s. Dividing by 3600 gives 5.56 hours, or 5.6 hours to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Using m = ZIt, time is 1/(5.0 × 10⁻⁷ × 100) = 20000 s. Dividing by 3600 gives 5.56 hours, or 5.6 hours to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements are true of isotopes of an element? I. Their neutral atoms have the same electron configuration and very similar chemical properties. II. They can be separated using differences in physical properties such as mass. III. Their nuclei have the same number of protons.
questions.ai_explanation: Isotopes have the same proton number. Their neutral atoms have the same electron configuration and very similar chemistry. Their different masses allow separation by physical methods such as mass separation.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same proton number. Their neutral atoms have the same electron configuration and very similar chemistry. Their different masses allow separation by physical methods such as mass separation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 4.0 g sample of a radioactive isotope has a half-life of 10 days. How long does it take for 3.5 g of the original isotope to decay?
questions.ai_explanation: If 3.5 g decays,0.5 g of the original radioactive isotope remains. The sequence is 4 →2 →1 →0.5 g: three half-lives. Therefore the time is 3 ×10 =30 days.
questions.explanation: If 3.5 g decays,0.5 g of the original radioactive isotope remains. The sequence is 4 →2 →1 →0.5 g: three half-lives. Therefore the time is 3 ×10 =30 days.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the energy-releasing proton-proton fusion chain, four protons, each of rest mass Mp, are converted into a helium nucleus X of rest mass Mx, along with other reaction products. Which relation is correct?
questions.ai_explanation: The proton-proton fusion chain produces a helium nucleus with less rest mass than the four initial protons. The rest-mass difference supplies the released energy and other reaction products, so 4 Mp > Mx.
questions.explanation: The proton-proton fusion chain produces a helium nucleus with less rest mass than the four initial protons. The rest-mass difference supplies the released energy and other reaction products, so 4 Mp > Mx.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements are true for alpha decay? I. Mass number decreases by four. II. Atomic number decreases by two. III. Mass number does not change.
questions.ai_explanation: An alpha particle contains two protons and two neutrons. Its emission reduces the parent’s mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2. Thus I and II are true, while III is false.
questions.explanation: An alpha particle contains two protons and two neutrons. Its emission reduces the parent’s mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2. Thus I and II are true, while III is false.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A ruler has divisions 1 cm apart. A single reading is rounded to the nearest division. What is the maximum magnitude of rounding error? Ignore other measurement errors.
questions.ai_explanation: When a reading is rounded to the nearest 1 cm division, it can differ from the true value by up to half a division. The rounding-error bound is therefore±0.5 cm.
questions.explanation: When a reading is rounded to the nearest 1 cm division, it can differ from the true value by up to half a division. The rounding-error bound is therefore±0.5 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a simple pendulum undergoing small oscillations, which quantities affect its period? I. Bob mass. II. Pendulum length. III. Gravitational acceleration.
questions.ai_explanation: For small oscillations, T =2π√(L/g). The period depends on length and gravitational acceleration, but not on bob mass. Thus II and III are the relevant quantities.
questions.explanation: For small oscillations, T =2π√(L/g). The period depends on length and gravitational acceleration, but not on bob mass. Thus II and III are the relevant quantities.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In an experiment measuring Young’s modulus of a circular wire, the tensile stress depends on the

options.B: Load and radius of the wire
options.C: Radius of the wire and extension
options.D: Extension and original length of the wire

questions.ai_explanation: Tensile stress is force divided by cross-sectional area. For a circular wire, stress =F/(πr²), so the load and radius determine it. Extension and original length instead determine strain.
questions.explanation: Tensile stress is force divided by cross-sectional area. For a circular wire, stress =F/(πr²), so the load and radius determine it. Extension and original length instead determine strain.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a plastic sphere floats in water (density = 1000 kg m-3) with 0.5 of its volume submerged and floats in oil with 0.4 volume submerged, the density of the oil is
questions.ai_explanation: Floating equilibrium gives sphere density =1000 ×0.5 =500 kg/m³. In the second liquid,500 =ρ ×0.4, so its density is 500/0.4 =1250 kg/m³.
questions.explanation: Floating equilibrium gives sphere density =1000 ×0.5 =500 kg/m³. In the second liquid,500 =ρ ×0.4, so its density is 500/0.4 =1250 kg/m³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At constant pressure, the density of a fixed mass of ideal gas is

options.C: Inversely proportional to its absolute temperature

questions.ai_explanation: At constant pressure, a fixed amount of ideal gas satisfies V/T =constant. Since density is mass divided by volume, density is inversely proportional to absolute temperature.
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, a fixed amount of ideal gas satisfies V/T =constant. Since density is mass divided by volume, density is inversely proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: How much heat is absorbed by 0.05 kg of copper, of specific heat capacity 390 J/(kg·K), when heated from 20 °C to 70 °C?
questions.ai_explanation: The temperature rise is 70 −20 =50 K. Heat absorbed is mcΔT =0.05 ×390 ×50 =975 J =9.75 ×10² J.
questions.explanation: The temperature rise is 70 −20 =50 K. Heat absorbed is mcΔT =0.05 ×390 ×50 =975 J =9.75 ×10² J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the sea?
questions.ai_explanation: Echo sounding sends a sound pulse downward and measures its return after reflection from the seabed. With sound speed v and round-trip time t, depth is vt/2.
questions.explanation: Echo sounding sends a sound pulse downward and measures its return after reflection from the seabed. With sound speed v and round-trip time t, depth is vt/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A siren disc has 32 equally spaced holes in one ring. A single air jet produces one pulse per passing hole. If the disc rotates at 25 revolutions per second, what is the sound frequency?
questions.ai_explanation: Each revolution lets 32 holes pass the air jet, producing 32 pressure pulses. At 25 revolutions per second, the pulse frequency is 32 ×25 =800 Hz.
questions.explanation: Each revolution lets 32 holes pass the air jet, producing 32 pressure pulses. At 25 revolutions per second, the pulse frequency is 32 ×25 =800 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following properties make the convex mirror useful as a driving mirror? I The image is real II The image is erect III It has a wide field of view IV The image is magnified
questions.ai_explanation: For objects in front of it, a convex mirror gives virtual, upright, diminished images. Its wide field of view lets a driver see more of the surrounding traffic. Therefore II and III apply.
questions.explanation: For objects in front of it, a convex mirror gives virtual, upright, diminished images. Its wide field of view lets a driver see more of the surrounding traffic. Therefore II and III apply.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed between the pole and focus of a concave mirror. The virtual image obtained is
questions.ai_explanation: An object between a concave mirror and its focus produces a virtual image behind the mirror. The image is upright and larger than the object.
questions.explanation: An object between a concave mirror and its focus produces a virtual image behind the mirror. The image is upright and larger than the object.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in air is 3.0 ×10⁸ m/s. Find its speed in glass of refractive index 1.50 relative to air.
questions.ai_explanation: The refractive index is the speed in air divided by the speed in glass. Thus v =3.0 ×10⁸/1.50 =2.0 ×10⁸ m/s.
questions.explanation: The refractive index is the speed in air divided by the speed in glass. Thus v =3.0 ×10⁸/1.50 =2.0 ×10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which arrangement gives the conventional order of these electromagnetic bands from shorter to longer typical wavelengths?

options.A: Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, x-rays, infra-red rays.
options.B: Gamma rays, x-rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays
options.C: Infra-red rays, ultraviolet rays, x-rays, gamma rays.
options.D: Gamma rays, ultraviolet rays, infra-red rays, x- rays.

questions.ai_explanation: In the conventional electromagnetic-spectrum order, gamma rays have the shortest typical wavelengths, followed by X-rays, ultraviolet and infrared.
questions.explanation: In the conventional electromagnetic-spectrum order, gamma rays have the shortest typical wavelengths, followed by X-rays, ultraviolet and infrared.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The angle between the direction of the earth’s magnetic field and the horizontal is called the
questions.ai_explanation: Magnetic dip, also called inclination, is the angle the magnetic field makes with the horizontal. Declination instead measures the horizontal difference between geographic and magnetic north.
questions.explanation: Magnetic dip, also called inclination, is the angle the magnetic field makes with the horizontal. Declination instead measures the horizontal difference between geographic and magnetic north.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Find the magnitude of the force on an electron of charge−1.6 ×10⁻¹⁹ C in an electric field of magnitude 10⁸ V/m.
questions.ai_explanation: Force magnitude is |q|E =(1.6 ×10⁻¹⁹)(10⁸) =1.6 ×10⁻¹¹ N. Because an electron is negatively charged, the force points opposite the electric field.
questions.explanation: Force magnitude is |q|E =(1.6 ×10⁻¹⁹)(10⁸) =1.6 ×10⁻¹¹ N. Because an electron is negatively charged, the force points opposite the electric field.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which change does not alter the equilibrium emf of a primary cell, with chemistry and other conditions otherwise unchanged?
questions.ai_explanation: Cell emf depends on electrode reactions, electrolyte conditions and temperature. Scaling up an otherwise identical cell increases available charge and can change internal resistance, but does not change its equilibrium emf.
questions.explanation: Cell emf depends on electrode reactions, electrolyte conditions and temperature. Scaling up an otherwise identical cell increases available charge and can change internal resistance, but does not change its equilibrium emf.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 5 V battery is connected across an initially uncharged 2.0 μF capacitor. After a long time, what is the magnitude of charge on either plate?
questions.ai_explanation: Charge magnitude on either plate is Q =CV =(2.0 ×10⁻⁶) ×5 =10 ×10⁻⁶ C =10 μC. The two plates carry equal and opposite charges.
questions.explanation: Charge magnitude on either plate is Q =CV =(2.0 ×10⁻⁶) ×5 =10 ×10⁻⁶ C =10 μC. The two plates carry equal and opposite charges.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For resistive devices with the same proportional protection margin, which has the smallest operating current and therefore needs the lowest fuse current rating?
questions.ai_explanation: Operating current is P/V. The four currents are 0.25 A,1.5 A,3.33 A and 8 A. The 60 W,240 V device draws the smallest current and needs the lowest current rating when the same protection margin is used.
questions.explanation: Operating current is P/V. The four currents are 0.25 A,1.5 A,3.33 A and 8 A. The 60 W,240 V device draws the smallest current and needs the lowest current rating when the same protection margin is used.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For steady current I through a constant resistance R for time t, the heat produced is

options.A: Inversely proportional to the current and the resistance
options.B: Directly proportional to the current, resistance and the time.
options.C: Inversely proportional to the square of the resistance, current and the time.
options.D: Directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time.

questions.ai_explanation: Joule heating is H =I²Rt for a steady current through a constant resistance. Heat is proportional to current squared, resistance and elapsed time.
questions.explanation: Joule heating is H =I²Rt for a steady current through a constant resistance. Heat is proportional to current squared, resistance and elapsed time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer has resistance 10 Ω and full-scale current 0.05 A. What added resistance converts it into a 100 V voltmeter, and how is it connected?
questions.ai_explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.
questions.explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The units of impedance, RMS voltage and resonance frequency are respectively
questions.ai_explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.
questions.explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal alternating current with peak I₀, which relation gives its RMS current Iᵣₘₛ?
questions.ai_explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.
questions.explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as the watt?
questions.ai_explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.
questions.explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two forces of 7 N and 3 N act at right angles. If θ is the angle between the resultant and the 7 N force, which relation holds?
questions.ai_explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.
questions.explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is projected at 80 m/s,30° above horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its maximum height above the launch point.
questions.ai_explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.
questions.explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An aeroplane lands at 180 km/h and slows uniformly to rest in 30 s. What distance does it cover before stopping?
questions.ai_explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.
questions.explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a fixed horizontal circle at constant angular velocity. Which statement is true?

options.A: Kinetic energy is constant but linear momentum varies
options.B: Linear momentum is constant but kinetic energy varies
options.C: Kinetic energy and linear momentum are both constant
options.D: Speed and linear velocity are both constant

questions.ai_explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.
questions.explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Starting with water stored at height, which sequence describes the main energy conversions when a hydroelectric station powers a lamp?
questions.ai_explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.
questions.explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object of mass 400 g and density 600 kg/m³ hangs at rest from a string with half its volume immersed in paraffin of density 900 kg/m³. Find the string tension. Use g =10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.
questions.explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: With its reference-junction temperature fixed, a thermocouple measures temperature through changes in its
questions.ai_explanation: With the reference junction held at a known temperature, a thermocouple’s emf changes with the measuring-junction temperature. Calibration relates that voltage to temperature.
questions.explanation: With the reference junction held at a known temperature, a thermocouple’s emf changes with the measuring-junction temperature. Calibration relates that voltage to temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed mass of ideal gas has its volume halved and absolute temperature doubled. What happens to its pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, P is proportional toT/V. Doubling absolute temperature while halving volume multiplies pressure by 2/(1/2) =4.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, P is proportional toT/V. Doubling absolute temperature while halving volume multiplies pressure by 2/(1/2) =4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Mix 200 g of water at 90 °C with 100 g of water at 30 °C. Neglect heat loss and the container’s heat capacity. What is the final temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.
questions.explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A solid melts at 80 °C. At that temperature,10⁵ J melts 10 g of the solid. Find its specific latent heat of fusion.
questions.ai_explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.
questions.explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stationary wave has wavelength 60 cm. Find the distance between consecutive antinodes.
questions.ai_explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.
questions.explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following waves can propagate through a vacuum?
questions.ai_explanation: Infrared radiation is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum. Sound, ultrasound and other acoustic waves need a material medium for their pressure disturbances.
questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum. Sound, ultrasound and other acoustic waves need a material medium for their pressure disturbances.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A radar pulse returns to its transmitting antenna 4 ×10⁻³ s after reflection from an aircraft. How far away is the aircraft? Use c =3 ×10⁸ m/s.
questions.ai_explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.
questions.explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A concave mirror of radius r forms a real image. Let u and v be the positive object and image distances. Which expression gives the magnitude of linear magnification?
questions.ai_explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.
questions.explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A thin camera lens has focal length 20 cm. An object is 100 cm from the lens. What lens-to-film distance gives a sharp image?
questions.ai_explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The property of the eye known as its power of accommodation is controlled by the
questions.ai_explanation: Ciliary muscles change tension in the supporting fibres of the lens. This changes lens curvature and optical power, allowing the eye to focus on objects at different distances.
questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles change tension in the supporting fibres of the lens. This changes lens curvature and optical power, allowing the eye to focus on objects at different distances.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly explain(s) why soft iron is preferred to steel in electromagnets? I Soft iron is more readily magnetized than steel. II Soft iron is more readily demagnetized than steel. III Soft iron retains magnetism more than steel.
questions.ai_explanation: Soft iron magnetizes readily when current flows and loses most of that magnetism when current stops. These properties make the electromagnet easy to switch on and off. Steel retains more magnetism.
questions.explanation: Soft iron magnetizes readily when current flows and loses most of that magnetism when current stops. These properties make the electromagnet easy to switch on and off. Steel retains more magnetism.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The terminal voltage of a battery is 4.0 V when supplying a current of 2.0 A, and 2.0 V when supplying a current of 3.0 A. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.ai_explanation: Terminal voltage is V =E −Ir. The voltage falls by 4 −2 =2 V when current rises by 3 −2 =1 A. Thus r =2/1 =2 Ω; both measurements then give emf 8 V.
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage is V =E −Ir. The voltage falls by 4 −2 =2 V when current rises by 3 −2 =1 A. Thus r =2/1 =2 Ω; both measurements then give emf 8 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 12 V ideal battery supplies a 1 Ω resistor in series with two parallel branches. Each branch contains two 2 Ω resistors in series. What is the total current supplied by the battery?
questions.ai_explanation: Each parallel branch has two 2 Ω resistors in series, giving 4 Ω per branch. Their parallel equivalent is 2 Ω. Adding the 1 Ω series resistor gives 3 Ω, so battery current is 12/3 =4 A.
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch has two 2 Ω resistors in series, giving 4 Ω per branch. Their parallel equivalent is 2 Ω. Adding the 1 Ω series resistor gives 3 Ω, so battery current is 12/3 =4 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 24 V ideal battery is connected across two parallel branches. One branch contains 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors in series; the other contains a 20 μF capacitor. All are initially uncharged. After charging, what is the voltage across the 5 μF capacitor?
questions.ai_explanation: The 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors are in series across 24 V. Their voltage drops are inversely proportional to capacitance, so the 5 μF capacitor gets 15/(5 +15) ×24 =18 V.
questions.explanation: The 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors are in series across 24 V. Their voltage drops are inversely proportional to capacitance, so the 5 μF capacitor gets 15/(5 +15) ×24 =18 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A resistive instrument rated 40 W has resistance 90 Ω. What operating voltage gives its rated power?
questions.ai_explanation: For a resistive instrument, P =V²/R. Therefore V =√(PR) =√(40 ×90) =√3600 =60 V.
questions.explanation: For a resistive instrument, P =V²/R. Therefore V =√(PR) =√(40 ×90) =√3600 =60 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a fixed transmitted power, the primary aim of high-voltage transmission is to

options.A: Minimize electrical energy losses due to heat production
options.B: Increase the rate of energy transfer by using high voltage
options.C: Increase the current in the wires.
options.D: Generate electricity at high current and low voltage.

questions.ai_explanation: For the same transmitted power, raising voltage reduces current. Since transmission-wire heating is I²R, the smaller current reduces wasted energy.
questions.explanation: For the same transmitted power, raising voltage reduces current. Since transmission-wire heating is I²R, the smaller current reduces wasted energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Find the inductive reactance of a 30.0 mH inductor at 1.30 ×10³ Hz, to one decimal place.
questions.ai_explanation: Inductive reactance is Xᴸ =2πfL. Converting 30.0 mH to 0.0300 H gives 2π ×1300 ×0.0300 =245.04… Ω, or 245.0 Ω to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is Xᴸ =2πfL. Converting 30.0 mH to 0.0300 H gives 2π ×1300 ×0.0300 =245.04… Ω, or 245.0 Ω to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements correctly describe cathode rays? I. They consist of small negatively charged particles. II. They can be deflected magnetically but not electrically. III. They consist of fast neutrons deflected by an electric field.
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which carry negative charge. An electric field can deflect them, and a magnetic field can deflect them when they have a velocity component perpendicular to it.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which carry negative charge. An electric field can deflect them, and a magnetic field can deflect them when they have a velocity component perpendicular to it.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the ordinary photoelectric effect, the threshold frequency depends on the

options.D: Collecting potential difference between cathode and anode

questions.ai_explanation: The threshold frequency is f₀ =φ/h, whereφ is the photocathode’s work function. It is therefore determined by the emitting material and its surface condition.
questions.explanation: The threshold frequency is f₀ =φ/h, whereφ is the photocathode’s work function. It is therefore determined by the emitting material and its surface condition.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: After three half-lives, what fraction of the original radioactive isotope has decayed?
questions.ai_explanation: After three half-lives, the fraction remaining is(1/2)³ =1/8. The fraction decayed is 1 −1/8 =7/8.
questions.explanation: After three half-lives, the fraction remaining is(1/2)³ =1/8. The fraction decayed is 1 −1/8 =7/8.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A nucleus has atomic number 88 and mass number 226. After two beta-minus decays and one alpha decay, which notation represents the final nucleus?
questions.ai_explanation: Each beta-minus decay raises atomic number by 1 without changing mass number. An alpha decay lowers mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2. The final numbers are A =226 −4 =222 and Z =88 +2 −2 =88.
questions.explanation: Each beta-minus decay raises atomic number by 1 without changing mass number. An alpha decay lowers mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2. The final numbers are A =226 −4 =222 and Z =88 +2 −2 =88.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a fixed metal surface in the ordinary photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons depends on the

options.C: Temperature of the radiation source alone

questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed metal surface, maximum photoelectron kinetic energy is Kmax =hf −φ. Increasing incident frequency above threshold raises the photon energy and therefore the maximum electron energy.
questions.explanation: For a fixed metal surface, maximum photoelectron kinetic energy is Kmax =hf −φ. Increasing incident frequency above threshold raises the photon energy and therefore the maximum electron energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform horizontal beam of weight 200 N and length 50 m is pivoted at one end. A cord at the other end makes 30° above the beam and holds it in equilibrium. Find the cord tension.
questions.ai_explanation: Taking moments about the pivot, the cord contributes T sin 30° ×L while the uniform beam’s weight contributes 200 ×L/2. Thus T ×0.5 =100, giving T =200 N.
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the pivot, the cord contributes T sin 30° ×L while the uniform beam’s weight contributes 200 ×L/2. Thus T ×0.5 =100, giving T =200 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 50 kg object is released from rest 2 m above the ground. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its kinetic energy just before impact.
questions.ai_explanation: Neglecting air resistance, gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic energy. Thus K =mgh =50 ×10 ×2 =1000 J just before impact.
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic energy. Thus K =mgh =50 ×10 ×2 =1000 J just before impact.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A horizontal force just starts a 20 kg object sliding on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.2. Find the force, using g = 10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: Just before sliding starts, the limiting friction is μₛN. The horizontal force leaves N = mg, so F = 0.2 × 20 × 10 = 40 N.
questions.explanation: Just before sliding starts, the limiting friction is μₛN. The horizontal force leaves N = mg, so F = 0.2 × 20 × 10 = 40 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a connected liquid of uniform density at rest, neglecting capillary effects, which statements are true? I. Pressure acts equally in all directions at a point. II. Pressure decreases with depth. III. Pressure at the same horizontal level is the same. IV. Pressure depends on the cross-sectional area of a barometer tube.
questions.ai_explanation: At a point in a liquid at rest, pressure acts equally in every direction. In a connected liquid of uniform density, equal depths have equal pressure. Pressure increases with depth and does not depend on tube area.
questions.explanation: At a point in a liquid at rest, pressure acts equally in every direction. In a connected liquid of uniform density, equal depths have equal pressure. Pressure increases with depth and does not depend on tube area.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The mass of a specific gravity bottle is 15.2 g when it is empty. It is 24.8 g when filled with kerosene and 27.2 g when filled with distilled water. Calculate the relative density of kerosene.
questions.ai_explanation: The kerosene mass is 24.8 − 15.2 = 9.6 g, and the water mass is 27.2 − 15.2 = 12.0 g. Equal bottle volumes give relative density 9.6/12.0 = 0.80.
questions.explanation: The kerosene mass is 24.8 − 15.2 = 9.6 g, and the water mass is 27.2 − 15.2 = 12.0 g. Equal bottle volumes give relative density 9.6/12.0 = 0.80.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a solid X floats in liquid P of relative density 2.0 and in liquid Q of relative density 1.5, it can be inferred that the

options.A: Weight of P displaced is greater than that of Q
options.B: Weight of P displaced is less than that of Q
options.C: Volume of P displaced is greater than that of Q
options.D: Volume of P displaced is less than that of Q

questions.ai_explanation: A floating object displaces its own weight of either liquid. Since P is denser, less of it is needed to provide that weight: Vₚ/Vq = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75.
questions.explanation: A floating object displaces its own weight of either liquid. Since P is denser, less of it is needed to provide that weight: Vₚ/Vq = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Convert 78 °C to kelvin, to the nearest kelvin.
questions.ai_explanation: Convert Celsius to kelvin by adding 273.15. Thus 78 °C is 351.15 K, which rounds to 351 K to the nearest kelvin.
questions.explanation: Convert Celsius to kelvin by adding 273.15. Thus 78 °C is 351.15 K, which rounds to 351 K to the nearest kelvin.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Mix 100 g of liquid L₁ at 78 °C with X grams of liquid L₂ at 50 °C. The final temperature is 66 °C. The specific heat capacity of L₂ is half that of L₁. Neglect heat loss and container heat capacity. Find X.
questions.ai_explanation: Heat lost equals heat gained: 100 c(78 − 66) = X(c/2)(66 − 50). Therefore 1200 c = 8 Xc, so X = 150 g.
questions.explanation: Heat lost equals heat gained: 100 c(78 − 66) = X(c/2)(66 − 50). Therefore 1200 c = 8 Xc, so X = 150 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A heater melts 100 g of ice at its melting point in 1 minute. Neglect heat losses and the test tube’s heat capacity. Find its power. Use latent heat of fusion 336 J/g.
questions.ai_explanation: Melting requires Q = mL = 100 × 336 = 33600 J. One minute is 60 s, so the required power is Q/t = 33600/60 = 560 W.
questions.explanation: Melting requires Q = mL = 100 × 336 = 33600 J. One minute is 60 s, so the required power is Q/t = 33600/60 = 560 W.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A transverse wave is y = 0.3 sin(0.5 x − 50 t), where x and y are in centimetres, t is in seconds, and the phase is in radians. What is the maximum displacement magnitude?
questions.ai_explanation: In y = A sin(kx − ωt), the sine varies between −1 and 1. The largest displacement magnitude is therefore A = 0.3 cm.
questions.explanation: In y = A sin(kx − ωt), the sine varies between −1 and 1. The largest displacement magnitude is therefore A = 0.3 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Sound travels from the surface to the sea bottom and returns after 4 s. If its speed is 1500 m/s, find the depth.
questions.ai_explanation: The echo makes a return trip, travelling twice the sea depth. Thus d = vt/2 = 1500 × 4/2 = 3000 m.
questions.explanation: The echo makes a return trip, travelling twice the sea depth. Thus d = vt/2 = 1500 × 4/2 = 3000 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which change halves the fundamental frequency of a stretched sonometer wire, with other relevant quantities held constant?

options.A: Double its vibrating length at fixed tension and mass per unit length
options.B: Double its mass at fixed vibrating length and tension
options.C: Halve its tension at fixed length and mass per unit length

questions.ai_explanation: For a stretched wire, f = (1/2 L)√(T/μ), where μ is mass per unit length. Doubling the vibrating length while holding tension and μ fixed halves the fundamental frequency.
questions.explanation: For a stretched wire, f = (1/2 L)√(T/μ), where μ is mass per unit length. Doubling the vibrating length while holding tension and μ fixed halves the fundamental frequency.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stretched string has fundamental frequency 400 Hz. Its vibrating length is doubled and its tension quadrupled, with mass per unit length unchanged. Find the new frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: Fundamental frequency is proportional to √T/L at fixed mass per unit length. The new frequency is 400 × √4/2 = 400 Hz.
questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency is proportional to √T/L at fixed mass per unit length. The new frequency is 400 × √4/2 = 400 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: To produce a parallel paraxial beam from a concave mirror, where should a small lamp be placed on its principal axis?

options.A: One focal length from the mirror
options.B: Two focal lengths from the mirror
options.C: At the image distance for an arbitrary object
options.D: Two radii of curvature from the mirror

questions.ai_explanation: A small lamp at a concave mirror’s principal focus sends rays that reflect parallel to the principal axis in the paraxial approximation. Its distance is therefore the focal length.
questions.explanation: A small lamp at a concave mirror’s principal focus sends rays that reflect parallel to the principal axis in the paraxial approximation. Its distance is therefore the focal length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Light of frequency 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz enters stationary glass of refractive index 1.5 from air. Find its frequency in the glass.
questions.ai_explanation: A stationary boundary does not change the light’s frequency. In glass, speed and wavelength decrease together, leaving frequency at 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
questions.explanation: A stationary boundary does not change the light’s frequency. In glass, speed and wavelength decrease together, leaving frequency at 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A converging thin lens of focal length 20 cm forms a virtual image with magnification 2. Find the object distance.
questions.ai_explanation: For an upright virtual image of magnification 2, v = −2 u. The thin-lens equation gives 1/20 =1/u −1/(2 u) =1/(2 u), so u =10 cm.
questions.explanation: For an upright virtual image of magnification 2, v = −2 u. The thin-lens equation gives 1/20 =1/u −1/(2 u) =1/(2 u), so u =10 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object touches the bottom of a glass block 3.0 cm thick, with refractive index 1.5. Viewed from air nearly normally through the top face, by how much does the object appear raised?
questions.ai_explanation: For near-normal viewing through a plane glass surface, apparent depth is real depth divided by refractive index:3.0/1.5 =2.0 cm. The object appears raised by 3.0 −2.0 =1.0 cm.
questions.explanation: For near-normal viewing through a plane glass surface, apparent depth is real depth divided by refractive index:3.0/1.5 =2.0 cm. The object appears raised by 3.0 −2.0 =1.0 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A projection lantern uses a converging lens of focal length f to make a real enlarged image on a screen. Its object distance u must satisfy
questions.ai_explanation: A projector needs a real enlarged image on a screen. A converging lens produces that image when the object is farther than f but nearer than 2 f.
