questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A plastic pen rubbed with dry silk attracts a small piece of paper. What happens to the pen and cloth during rubbing?

options.A: Both the pen and the cloth are magnetized
options.B: The pen is magnetized but the cloth is not
options.C: The pen is charged while the cloth is magnetized
options.D: Both the pen and the cloth are charged.

questions.ai_explanation: Rubbing transfers electric charge between the pen and cloth, leaving opposite charges on them. The charged pen polarizes nearby neutral paper, and the nearer opposite charge is attracted more strongly.
questions.explanation: Rubbing transfers electric charge between the pen and cloth, leaving opposite charges on them. The charged pen polarizes nearby neutral paper, and the nearer opposite charge is attracted more strongly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Resistors R₁ =4 Ω and R₂ =5 Ω are in parallel across the same voltage. Find P₁:P₂.
questions.ai_explanation: Parallel resistors have the same voltage. Since P = V²/R, their power ratio is P₁/P₂ = R₂/R₁ =5/4, giving 5:4.
questions.explanation: Parallel resistors have the same voltage. Since P = V²/R, their power ratio is P₁/P₂ = R₂/R₁ =5/4, giving 5:4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω supplies two parallel resistors, 12 Ω and 6 Ω. Find the magnitude of current in the 12 Ω resistor.
questions.ai_explanation: The parallel equivalent is 12 ×6/(12 +6) =4 Ω. Including internal resistance gives 5 Ω, so total current is 12/5 =2.4 A. Terminal voltage is 2.4 ×4 =9.6 V, giving 9.6/12 =0.8 A in the 12 Ω resistor.
questions.explanation: The parallel equivalent is 12 ×6/(12 +6) =4 Ω. Including internal resistance gives 5 Ω, so total current is 12/5 =2.4 A. Terminal voltage is 2.4 ×4 =9.6 V, giving 9.6/12 =0.8 A in the 12 Ω resistor.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If two parallel conductors carry currents flowing in the same direction, the conductors will

options.C: Both move in the same direction
options.D: Have no effect on each other.

questions.ai_explanation: Each conductor produces a magnetic field at the other. Applying the magnetic-force direction rule to parallel currents in the same direction gives a force on each wire toward the other.
questions.explanation: Each conductor produces a magnetic field at the other. Applying the magnetic-force direction rule to parallel currents in the same direction gives a force on each wire toward the other.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A sinusoidal alternating voltage has frequency 50 Hz. P is an upward zero crossing and R is the immediately following downward zero crossing. Find the time from P to R.
questions.ai_explanation: Consecutive zero crossings with opposite slopes are half a cycle apart. At 50 Hz, a cycle lasts 1/50 s, so the interval is 1/100 s.
questions.explanation: Consecutive zero crossings with opposite slopes are half a cycle apart. At 50 Hz, a cycle lasts 1/50 s, so the interval is 1/100 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, light of photon energy 2 eV falls on a metal of work function 3 eV. What happens?

options.B: A few electrons emerge with maximum kinetic energy 1 eV
options.C: A few electrons emerge with maximum kinetic energy 3 eV

questions.ai_explanation: A photon must supply at least the work function to liberate an electron. Here 2 eV is less than 3 eV, so ordinary single-photon photoemission does not occur.
questions.explanation: A photon must supply at least the work function to liberate an electron. Here 2 eV is less than 3 eV, so ordinary single-photon photoemission does not occur.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the dimension of pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. Force has dimensions MLT⁻² and area L², so pressure has dimensions ML⁻¹T⁻².
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. Force has dimensions MLT⁻² and area L², so pressure has dimensions ML⁻¹T⁻².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A simple pendulum at small amplitude passes its lowest point twice per second. Find its length to two decimal places, using g =10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: A pendulum crosses its lowest point twice per complete oscillation, so two crossings per second mean period 1 s. From T =2π√(L/g), L =10/(4π²) =0.253… m, or 0.25 m to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: A pendulum crosses its lowest point twice per complete oscillation, so two crossings per second mean period 1 s. From T =2π√(L/g), L =10/(4π²) =0.253… m, or 0.25 m to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three non-collinear points are O, A and B. Vector P runs from O to A, Q from O to B, and R from B to A. Which relation is correct?
questions.ai_explanation: Following Q from O to B and then R from B to A reaches the same endpoint as P from O to A. Therefore P =Q +R.
questions.explanation: Following Q from O to B and then R from B to A reaches the same endpoint as P from O to A. Therefore P =Q +R.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20 N load is held at rest by two symmetric cords, each making 30° above horizontal. Find the tension T in each cord.
questions.ai_explanation: The two equal tensions each make 30° above horizontal. Horizontal components cancel, while vertical balance gives 2 T sin 30° =20 N. Since sin 30° =1/2, T =20 N.
questions.explanation: The two equal tensions each make 30° above horizontal. Horizontal components cancel, while vertical balance gives 2 T sin 30° =20 N. Since sin 30° =1/2, T =20 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a ball rolls on a smooth level ground, the motion of its centre is
questions.ai_explanation: The centre of a rolling ball moves along the ground as the ball changes position. This is translational motion; rotation describes the ball turning about its centre.
questions.explanation: The centre of a rolling ball moves along the ground as the ball changes position. This is translational motion; rotation describes the ball turning about its centre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20 kg block on a smooth 30° incline is joined by a light inextensible string over a frictionless massless pulley to a hanging 30 kg mass. Use g =10 m/s². Find the acceleration magnitude.
questions.ai_explanation: The hanging weight is 30 ×10 =300 N. The 20 kg block’s downslope weight component is 20 ×10 sin 30° =100 N. The net driving force is 200 N on 50 kg, so a =4 m/s².
questions.explanation: The hanging weight is 30 ×10 =300 N. The 20 kg block’s downslope weight component is 20 ×10 sin 30° =100 N. The net driving force is 200 N on 50 kg, so a =4 m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Approximate lunar surface gravity as one-sixth of Earth’s. If Earth’s gravity is 10 m/s², find lunar gravity to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Using the usual approximation that lunar surface gravity is one-sixth of Earth’s gives gmoon =10/6 =1.666… m/s², or 1.67 m/s².
questions.explanation: Using the usual approximation that lunar surface gravity is one-sixth of Earth’s gives gmoon =10/6 =1.666… m/s², or 1.67 m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A wire obeying Hooke’s law is extended by 0.02 m from its unstretched length by a final force of 500 N. Find its stored elastic energy.
questions.ai_explanation: For a Hooke’s-law wire, force rises linearly from zero to 500 N over the 0.02 m extension. Stored energy is the triangular area under the force-extension graph:½ ×500 ×0.02 =5 J.
questions.explanation: For a Hooke’s-law wire, force rises linearly from zero to 500 N over the 0.02 m extension. Stored energy is the triangular area under the force-extension graph:½ ×500 ×0.02 =5 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed amount of air in a bubble rises slowly through a lake at constant temperature. Neglect surface-tension effects. Its volume increases because

options.A: Atmospheric pressure acts on the surface of the lake.
options.B: Pressure increases with depth of the lake.

questions.ai_explanation: Water pressure is higher at greater depth. As the bubble rises, external pressure falls. At constant temperature a fixed amount of gas expands as its pressure decreases, according to Boyle’s law.
questions.explanation: Water pressure is higher at greater depth. As the bubble rises, external pressure falls. At constant temperature a fixed amount of gas expands as its pressure decreases, according to Boyle’s law.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the classical ideal-gas model, absolute temperature is a measure of the

options.A: Total heat transferred to the gas
options.B: Mean translational kinetic energy per molecule
options.C: Kinetic energy of one particular molecule
options.D: Total work done by the molecules

questions.ai_explanation: For a classical ideal gas, average translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3 kT/2. Temperature therefore measures this average, rather than the energy of a particular molecule or total heat transfer.
questions.explanation: For a classical ideal gas, average translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3 kT/2. Temperature therefore measures this average, rather than the energy of a particular molecule or total heat transfer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An ideal 2000 W kettle heats 2.0 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C. Neglect kettle heat capacity and heat loss. With water’s specific heat capacity 4200 J/(kg·K), how long does this take?
questions.ai_explanation: The temperature rise is 100 −20 =80 K. Heating needs Q =mcΔT =2.0 ×4200 ×80 =672000 J. At 2000 W, the time is 672000/2000 =336 s.
questions.explanation: The temperature rise is 100 −20 =80 K. Heating needs Q =mcΔT =2.0 ×4200 ×80 =672000 J. At 2000 W, the time is 672000/2000 =336 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the exclusive property of a transverse wave?
questions.ai_explanation: Polarization selects the direction of oscillation in the plane perpendicular to travel. That directional freedom belongs to transverse waves; a purely longitudinal wave oscillates along its travel direction.
questions.explanation: Polarization selects the direction of oscillation in the plane perpendicular to travel. That directional freedom belongs to transverse waves; a purely longitudinal wave oscillates along its travel direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A radio signal has wavelength 1500 m and frequency 200 kHz. At the same wave speed, what wavelength corresponds to 1000 kHz?
questions.ai_explanation: The wave speed is fλ =200000 ×1500 =3 ×10⁸ m/s. At 1000000 Hz, the wavelength is 3 ×10⁸/10⁶ =300 m.
questions.explanation: The wave speed is fλ =200000 ×1500 =3 ×10⁸ m/s. At 1000000 Hz, the wavelength is 3 ×10⁸/10⁶ =300 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The difference between sound waves and light waves is that sound waves

options.A: Are transverse while light waves are longitudinal.
options.B: Require a medium to travel while light waves do not.
options.C: Can be diffracted but light waves cannot
options.D: Cannot be reflected but light waves can.

questions.ai_explanation: Sound consists of mechanical disturbances of a material medium. Light is electromagnetic radiation and can propagate through vacuum, so it does not require matter along its path.
questions.explanation: Sound consists of mechanical disturbances of a material medium. Light is electromagnetic radiation and can propagate through vacuum, so it does not require matter along its path.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a steady simple acoustic tone, its pitch is increased primarily by
questions.ai_explanation: For a steady simple tone, a higher vibration frequency is heard as a higher pitch. Changing amplitude mainly changes loudness rather than the tone’s frequency.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: During a total solar eclipse observed from Earth, which arrangement holds?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of colours gives the widest separation in the spectrum of white light?

questions.question: Parallel plates are 8.0 ×10⁻³ m apart at a potential difference of 600 V, with the negative plate earthed. Neglect edge effects. Find the electric-field magnitude.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Earth’s magnetic field at different surface locations?

options.A: The same in magnitude and direction
options.B: The same in magnitude but different in direction
options.C: Different in both magnitude and direction

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A resistor’s resistance is halved and its applied voltage tripled. Find the ratio of its new current to its original current.

questions.explanation: Ohm’s law gives I =V/R. Tripling voltage and halving resistance gives Inew =3 V/(R/2) =6 V/R, so the new-to-old current ratio is 6:1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected across a cable of resistance 1.0 Ω. Find the current.
questions.ai_explanation: The battery’s internal resistance is in series with the cable. Total resistance is 0.5 +1.0 =1.5 Ω, giving I =12/1.5 =8.0 A.
questions.explanation: The battery’s internal resistance is in series with the cable. Total resistance is 0.5 +1.0 =1.5 Ω, giving I =12/1.5 =8.0 A.

questions.question: A capacitor network between two terminals has these sections in series: 2 μF, 3 μF, a parallel pair of 2 μF and 4 μF, then 4 μF. Find the equivalent capacitance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The maximum voltage magnitude across a 100 Ω resistor is 20 V. Find its maximum instantaneous power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns and 100 secondary turns. With 12 V AC applied to the primary, what is the secondary voltage, using the same voltage convention?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A particle’s position is x =10 +12 t² metres, with time t in seconds. Find its average speed from t =2 s to t =5 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 5 kg block is released on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to horizontal. Find its downslope acceleration using g =10 m/s².

questions.question: An arrow of mass 0.1 kg travelling horizontally at 15 m/s embeds in a stationary 0.4 kg block on a smooth horizontal surface. Find their common speed.

questions.explanation: Horizontal momentum is conserved as the arrow embeds in the block. Thus 0.1 ×15 =(0.1 +0.4)v, giving v =1.5/0.5 =3.0 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a body in simple harmonic motion, which quantities are in phase?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two point masses attract with force 10⁻⁴ N at separation 0.18 m. Find the force when their separation is 0.06 m.
questions.ai_explanation: Gravitational force varies inversely with separation squared. Reducing distance from 0.18 m to 0.06 m multiplies the force by(0.18/0.06)² =9, giving 9.0 ×10⁻⁴ N.
questions.explanation: Gravitational force varies inversely with separation squared. Reducing distance from 0.18 m to 0.06 m multiplies the force by(0.18/0.06)² =9, giving 9.0 ×10⁻⁴ N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three forces act on a particle at rest: 6 N vertically downward, 6√3 N horizontally right, and 12 N upward-left along a cord. The cord makes angle θ with the vertical. Find θ.

questions.explanation: Vertical equilibrium requires the upward component 12 cosθ to equal 6 N. Thus cosθ =1/2 and θ =60°. The horizontal component is 12 sin 60° =6√3 N, matching the rightward force.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An empty 60 litre tank has mass 10 kg. Find its mass when full of fuel of relative density 0.72. Use water density 1000 kg/m³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A mercury thermometer’s thread lengths at 0 °C, 100 °C and an unknown temperature are 25 mm, 225 mm and 175 mm respectively. Assuming linear calibration, find the unknown temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed amount of ideal gas in a tyre has absolute pressure 3 ×10⁵ Pa at 27 °C. At constant volume its absolute pressure rises to 4 ×10⁵ Pa. Find the final Celsius temperature, using K = °C +273.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At ordinary atmospheric pressure, a fixed mass of pure ice melts completely to water at 0 °C. Which description is correct?

options.A: Latent heat is absorbed, the mass remains constant and the volume decreases.
options.B: Latent heat is given out, the mass remains constant and the volume decreases.
options.C: Latent heat is given out, the mass increases and the volume remains constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Adding dilute hydrochloric acid to an aqueous solution of a crystalline salt gives a yellow precipitate and a gas that turns acidified dichromate paper green. Which salt is most likely?

questions.question: Which option most precisely describes the direct role of sodium chloride added during soap preparation?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many chlorine atoms are present in 5.85 g of NaCl? [Na = 23, Cl = 35.5; Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The molar mass of NaCl is 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g mol⁻¹. Therefore 5.85 g contains 0.100 mol NaCl. Each formula unit contains one chlorine atom, so the number of chlorine atoms is 0.100 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².
questions.explanation: The molar mass of NaCl is 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g mol⁻¹. Therefore 5.85 g contains 0.100 mol NaCl. Each formula unit contains one chlorine atom, so the number of chlorine atoms is 0.100 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².

questions.question: What mass of magnesium reacts completely with 250 cm³ of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ HCl? [Mg = 24]
questions.ai_explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. The acid amount is 0.250 × 0.5 = 0.125 mol. Half as many moles of magnesium are needed: 0.0625 mol. Its mass is 0.0625 × 24 = 1.5 g.
questions.explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. The acid amount is 0.250 × 0.5 = 0.125 mol. Half as many moles of magnesium are needed: 0.0625 mol. Its mass is 0.0625 × 24 = 1.5 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Oxygen occupies a fixed 2.76 litre container at 0.825 atm and 300 K. Half the amount of gas is removed while the temperature remains 300 K. What pressure does the remaining gas exert?
questions.ai_explanation: For an ideal gas at constant volume and temperature, P = nRT/V, so pressure is proportional to the amount of gas. Halving the amount halves the pressure: 0.825/2 = 0.4125 atm, which rounds to 0.413 atm.
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant volume and temperature, P = nRT/V, so pressure is proportional to the amount of gas. Halving the amount halves the pressure: 0.825/2 = 0.4125 atm, which rounds to 0.413 atm.

questions.explanation: At equal temperature and pressure, vapour density is proportional to molar mass. Ethanal, C₂H₄O, has molar mass 44; ethanoic acid and propanol each have 60, and dichloromethane has 85. Ethanal therefore has the lowest vapour density.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The solubility of Na₃AsO₄·12H₂O is 38.9 g per 100 g of water. What is the mass percentage of Na₃AsO₄ in the saturated solution? [Na = 23, As = 75, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: Na₃AsO₄ has molar mass 3×23 + 75 + 4×16 = 208 g mol⁻¹. The hydrate has mass 208 + 12×18 = 424 g mol⁻¹. Thus 38.9 g hydrate contains 38.9×208/424 = 19.08 g Na₃AsO₄. The solution mass is 100 + 38.9 = 138.9 g, giving 19.08/138.9×100 = 13.7%.
questions.explanation: Na₃AsO₄ has molar mass 3×23 + 75 + 4×16 = 208 g mol⁻¹. The hydrate has mass 208 + 12×18 = 424 g mol⁻¹. Thus 38.9 g hydrate contains 38.9×208/424 = 19.08 g Na₃AsO₄. The solution mass is 100 + 38.9 = 138.9 g, giving 19.08/138.9×100 = 13.7%.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which pair of reported observations is correct for fresh lime juice and ethanol respectively?

questions.explanation: HCl and NaOH react in a 1:1 mole ratio. At equivalence, c(HCl) = 0.15 × 24.83/39.45 = 0.09441 mol dm⁻³, corresponding to 0.094 mol dm⁻³.

questions.question: What mass of magnesium is deposited when 2 A flows for 2 hours 30 minutes through molten MgCl₂? Assume 100% current efficiency. [Mg = 24; F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For 3CuO + 2NH₃ → 3Cu + 3H₂O + N₂, how many electrons are transferred per mole of copper produced? Use Avogadro constant 6.0 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.

questions.explanation: Copper in CuO has oxidation state +2 and gains two electrons to become Cu. One mole of copper therefore requires two moles of electrons: 2×6.0×10²³ = 1.2×10²⁴ electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Dissolving 5 g of NH₄NO₃ in water absorbs 1.6 kJ from the water and container. What is its molar enthalpy of solution? [N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]

questions.question: Calculate the enthalpy change for SO₃(g) + H₂O(l) → H₂SO₄(l), given formation enthalpies of −395, −286 and −811 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively.

questions.question: A compound forms between trivalent metal M and tetravalent non-metal X. What is its simplest formula?
questions.ai_explanation: The combining capacities must balance. Four atoms of a trivalent element provide 4×3 = 12 valence units; three atoms of a tetravalent element provide 3×4 = 12. The simplest ratio is therefore M₄X₃.

questions.question: A volatile compound has carbon-to-hydrogen mole ratio 1:2. A 0.12 g sample gives 32 cm³ of vapour at STP. What is its molecular formula? [Molar gas volume = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹; C = 12, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: The empirical formula from C:H = 1:2 is CH₂, with mass 14. The vapour amount is 0.032/22.4 mol, giving molar mass 0.12/(0.032/22.4) = 84 g mol⁻¹. Since 84/14 = 6, the molecular formula is C₆H₁₂.
questions.explanation: The empirical formula from C:H = 1:2 is CH₂, with mass 14. The vapour amount is 0.032/22.4 mol, giving molar mass 0.12/(0.032/22.4) = 84 g mol⁻¹. Since 84/14 = 6, the molecular formula is C₆H₁₂.

questions.question: What volume of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ H₃PO₄ is required for complete neutralisation with 45.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?

questions.question: How is aluminium extracted commercially from its ore?

questions.ai_explanation: The ore contains 80×0.700 = 56.0 kg of Fe₂O₃. Iron contributes 2×56 = 112 of its relative formula mass 160. The theoretical iron mass is therefore 56.0×112/160 = 39.2 kg.
questions.explanation: The ore contains 80×0.700 = 56.0 kg of Fe₂O₃. Iron contributes 2×56 = 112 of its relative formula mass 160. The theoretical iron mass is therefore 56.0×112/160 = 39.2 kg.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In two experiments, 0.36 g and 0.71 g of chlorine combine with 0.20 g and 0.40 g of a metal X, respectively. Which law is supported by these mass data, allowing for their reported precision?
questions.ai_explanation: The chlorine-to-metal mass ratios are 0.36/0.20 = 1.80 and 0.71/0.40 = 1.775. These are approximately the same at the precision of the reported masses. The data therefore support constant composition: the elements combine in essentially the same mass proportion.
questions.explanation: The chlorine-to-metal mass ratios are 0.36/0.20 = 1.80 and 0.71/0.40 = 1.775. These are approximately the same at the precision of the reported masses. The data therefore support constant composition: the elements combine in essentially the same mass proportion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of CO₂ at STP is produced by complete thermal decomposition of 1 kg of KHCO₃? [K = 39, H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar gas volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The balanced decomposition is 2KHCO₃ → K₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. KHCO₃ has molar mass 100 g mol⁻¹, so 1 kg is 10 mol. Every two moles give one mole of CO₂; 5 mol therefore occupy 5×22.4 = 112 dm³ at STP.
questions.explanation: The balanced decomposition is 2KHCO₃ → K₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. KHCO₃ has molar mass 100 g mol⁻¹, so 1 kg is 10 mol. Every two moles give one mole of CO₂; 5 mol therefore occupy 5×22.4 = 112 dm³ at STP.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Atoms of X have two outer-shell electrons and atoms of Y have seven. For their expected ionic compound, which statement is false?

options.B: It is likely to be ionic

questions.ai_explanation: In the expected electron-transfer model, X loses two electrons to form X²⁺ and each Y gains one to form Y⁻. Charge balance requires two Y⁻ ions for each X²⁺, giving XY₂. A formula of XY would not be electrically neutral.
questions.explanation: In the expected electron-transfer model, X loses two electrons to form X²⁺ and each Y gains one to form Y⁻. Charge balance requires two Y⁻ ions for each X²⁺, giving XY₂. A formula of XY would not be electrically neutral.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: X⁻ and Y⁺ each contain 10 electrons. How many protons are in the nuclei of X and Y, respectively?
questions.ai_explanation: An X⁻ ion has gained one electron, so its 10 electrons correspond to 9 protons. A Y⁺ ion has lost one electron, so its 10 electrons correspond to 11 protons. Ion formation changes electron count, not the number of protons in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: An X⁻ ion has gained one electron, so its 10 electrons correspond to 9 protons. A Y⁺ ion has lost one electron, so its 10 electrons correspond to 11 protons. Ion formation changes electron count, not the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed combination describes bonding in ammonium chloride, including the electron-pair donation used to form NH₄⁺?
questions.ai_explanation: Ammonium chloride is an ionic solid of NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Within NH₄⁺, the N–H bonds are covalent; formation from NH₃ and H⁺ can be described as donation of a nitrogen lone pair, or dative covalent bonding. Once NH₄⁺ has formed, its four N–H bonds are equivalent.
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is an ionic solid of NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. Within NH₄⁺, the N–H bonds are covalent; formation from NH₃ and H⁺ can be described as donation of a nitrogen lone pair, or dative covalent bonding. Once NH₄⁺ has formed, its four N–H bonds are equivalent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which sequence is in increasing order of electronegativity?
questions.ai_explanation: All five elements lie in period 3. Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across this period, so the order is Na < Mg < Al < P < Cl. Chlorine attracts shared bonding electrons most strongly in this list.
questions.explanation: All five elements lie in period 3. Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across this period, so the order is Na < Mg < Al < P < Cl. Chlorine attracts shared bonding electrons most strongly in this list.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed ion is a particularly toxic drinking-water contaminant at low concentrations?
questions.ai_explanation: Mercury ions are toxic contaminants and are a concern in drinking water at low concentrations. Calcium and magnesium commonly contribute to water hardness, while iron can affect colour and taste. Mercury is the toxic-metal contaminant identified by this comparison.
questions.explanation: Mercury ions are toxic contaminants and are a concern in drinking water at low concentrations. Calcium and magnesium commonly contribute to water hardness, while iron can affect colour and taste. Mercury is the toxic-metal contaminant identified by this comparison.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of CO₂ at STP results when 10 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ Na₂CO₃ solution reacts with excess acid? [Molar gas volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The carbonate amount is 0.1×(10/1000) = 0.001 mol. Acid converts each CO₃²⁻ into one CO₂ molecule, so the CO₂ amount is also 0.001 mol. Its STP volume is 0.001×22.4 = 0.0224 dm³, or 22.4 cm³.
questions.explanation: The carbonate amount is 0.1×(10/1000) = 0.001 mol. Acid converts each CO₃²⁻ into one CO₂ molecule, so the CO₂ amount is also 0.001 mol. Its STP volume is 0.001×22.4 = 0.0224 dm³, or 22.4 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 2H₂S(g) + SO₂(g) → 3S(s) + 2H₂O(l). Which statement describes this reaction?

options.A: It is redox: H₂S is the oxidant and SO₂ is the reductant
options.B: It is redox: SO₂ is the oxidant and H₂S is the reductant
options.C: It is not redox because there is no oxidant
options.D: It is not redox because there is no reductant

questions.ai_explanation: Sulfur in H₂S changes from −2 to 0, so H₂S is oxidised and acts as the reductant. Sulfur in SO₂ changes from +4 to 0, so SO₂ is reduced and acts as the oxidant. Two sulfide sulfur atoms each lose two electrons, balancing the four electrons gained by the SO₂ sulfur atom.
questions.explanation: Sulfur in H₂S changes from −2 to 0, so H₂S is oxidised and acts as the reductant. Sulfur in SO₂ changes from +4 to 0, so SO₂ is reduced and acts as the oxidant. Two sulfide sulfur atoms each lose two electrons, balancing the four electrons gained by the SO₂ sulfur atom.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: MnO₂ hastens hydrogen peroxide decomposition mainly by

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: NO(g) + CO(g) ⇌ ½N₂(g) + CO₂(g), ΔH = −89.3 kJ. Which conditions favour the greatest equilibrium conversion of NO and CO to products?
questions.ai_explanation: The negative enthalpy change means the forward reaction releases heat, so lowering temperature favours products. There are 2 moles of reactant gases and 1.5 moles of product gases per equation. Higher pressure therefore also favours products, which occupy the smaller gas volume.

There are 2 moles of reactant gases and 1.5 moles of product gases per equation. Higher pressure therefore also favours products, which occupy the smaller gas volume.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, doubling the initial NO concentration from the first measurement to the second changes the initial rate of its reaction with chlorine from 3.0×10⁻⁵ to 1.2×10⁻⁴ mol s⁻¹. By what factor does the rate increase?
questions.ai_explanation: The rate ratio is (1.2×10⁻⁴)/(3.0×10⁻⁵) = 4. Thus, when the listed initial NO concentration doubles, the measured initial rate increases fourfold.
questions.explanation: The rate ratio is (1.2×10⁻⁴)/(3.0×10⁻⁵) = 4. Thus, when the listed initial NO concentration doubles, the measured initial rate increases fourfold.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed gas can rekindle a brightly glowing splint?
questions.ai_explanation: Nitrous oxide, N₂O, can support combustion and relight a glowing splint. At the hot splint it can decompose to nitrogen and oxygen. The glowing-splint observation is therefore not exclusive to a sample of pure oxygen.
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide, N₂O, can support combustion and relight a glowing splint. At the hot splint it can decompose to nitrogen and oxygen. The glowing-splint observation is therefore not exclusive to a sample of pure oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed salt can be melted without decomposition under ordinary laboratory conditions?
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium carbonate is thermally stable enough to melt during ordinary heating. Calcium, magnesium and zinc carbonates instead undergo thermal decomposition to their oxides and carbon dioxide before they can simply be melted under ordinary laboratory conditions.
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate is thermally stable enough to melt during ordinary heating. Calcium, magnesium and zinc carbonates instead undergo thermal decomposition to their oxides and carbon dioxide before they can simply be melted under ordinary laboratory conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why does the white precipitate produced by adding aqueous ammonia to Zn²⁺ solution dissolve in excess ammonia?

options.C: Zinc forms a complex soluble in excess ammonia
options.D: Ammonia solution is a strong base

questions.ai_explanation: Aqueous ammonia first supplies hydroxide ions, forming white Zn(OH)₂. In excess ammonia, zinc forms the soluble complex ion [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺, so the precipitate dissolves. This ligand-complex formation explains the observation.
questions.explanation: Aqueous ammonia first supplies hydroxide ions, forming white Zn(OH)₂. In excess ammonia, zinc forms the soluble complex ion [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺, so the precipitate dissolves. This ligand-complex formation explains the observation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which substance in clear aqueous solution forms a white precipitate when CO₂ is bubbled through it for a short time?
questions.ai_explanation: A small amount of CO₂ reacts with limewater, Ca(OH)₂(aq), to form insoluble calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O. The CaCO₃ is the white precipitate. With prolonged excess CO₂, that precipitate can dissolve again.
questions.explanation: A small amount of CO₂ reacts with limewater, Ca(OH)₂(aq), to form insoluble calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O. The CaCO₃ is the white precipitate. With prolonged excess CO₂, that precipitate can dissolve again.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which pair of metals can be obtained by thermal decomposition of their nitrate salts?
questions.ai_explanation: Silver and mercury nitrates can ultimately yield their metals on strong heating because the corresponding oxides are thermally unstable. Copper and magnesium nitrates instead leave stable metal oxides under the usual comparison conditions. The pair is therefore mercury and silver.
questions.explanation: Silver and mercury nitrates can ultimately yield their metals on strong heating because the corresponding oxides are thermally unstable. Copper and magnesium nitrates instead leave stable metal oxides under the usual comparison conditions. The pair is therefore mercury and silver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which compound can exist as geometric isomers?
questions.ai_explanation: Each carbon of the double bond in but-2-ene has one H and one CH₃ group. Restricted rotation allows distinct cis and trans arrangements. But-1-ene and 2-methylbut-2-ene have identical groups on one double-bond carbon, while CH₂BrCl has no double bond.
questions.explanation: Each carbon of the double bond in but-2-ene has one H and one CH₃ group. Restricted rotation allows distinct cis and trans arrangements. But-1-ene and 2-methylbut-2-ene have identical groups on one double-bond carbon, while CH₂BrCl has no double bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What mass of bromine is required for complete addition to 10 g of propyne? [C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80]
questions.ai_explanation: Propyne has molar mass 3×12 + 4×1 = 40 g mol⁻¹, so 10 g is 0.25 mol. Complete addition across its triple bond uses 2 mol of Br₂ per mole of propyne. The bromine mass is 0.25×2×160 = 80 g.
questions.explanation: Propyne has molar mass 3×12 + 4×1 = 40 g mol⁻¹, so 10 g is 0.25 mol. Complete addition across its triple bond uses 2 mol of Br₂ per mole of propyne. The bromine mass is 0.25×2×160 = 80 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethene is absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄. The product is diluted with water and warmed. Which organic product is formed?
questions.ai_explanation: Ethene first adds sulfuric acid to form ethyl hydrogen sulfate. Adding water and warming hydrolyses this intermediate to ethanol and regenerates sulfuric acid. The overall change adds H and OH across the ethene double bond.
questions.explanation: Ethene first adds sulfuric acid to form ethyl hydrogen sulfate. Adding water and warming hydrolyses this intermediate to ethanol and regenerates sulfuric acid. The overall change adds H and OH across the ethene double bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is an advantage of common soapless detergents over soap in hard water?

options.A: They are always easier to manufacture
options.B: They always foam more than soap
options.C: Their salts with hard-water ions remain soluble
options.D: They always kill more germs than soap

questions.ai_explanation: Soap forms insoluble calcium and magnesium salts, seen as scum in hard water. Common soapless detergents avoid this precipitation because their corresponding salts remain sufficiently soluble. They therefore retain cleaning action better in hard water.
questions.explanation: Soap forms insoluble calcium and magnesium salts, seen as scum in hard water. Common soapless detergents avoid this precipitation because their corresponding salts remain sufficiently soluble. They therefore retain cleaning action better in hard water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂Cl?
questions.ai_explanation: The longest carbon chain has three atoms. Numbering from CH₂Cl places chlorine at carbon 1 and the methyl branch at carbon 2. The compound is 1-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed pair is produced by the chlorination of CH₃COOH with Cl₂ in sunlight?
questions.ai_explanation: In the first chlorination step, one hydrogen on the methyl group of ethanoic acid is replaced by chlorine. The products are chloroethanoic acid, ClCH₂COOH, and HCl. The carboxyl group remains intact.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why can a metal have a large temperature interval between melting and boiling?

options.A: All metals have very high melting points
options.C: Metallic cohesion remains in the liquid, while boiling separates the atoms
options.D: Metal crystal lattices are easily broken

questions.ai_explanation: Liquid metal still has strong attraction between its atoms and delocalised electrons. Melting permits atoms to move past one another, while boiling separates them into the gas phase and overcomes much more of this cohesion. This helps explain why vaporisation needs much more energy.
questions.explanation: Liquid metal still has strong attraction between its atoms and delocalised electrons. questions.question: Which listed substance is a mixture?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many moles of O₂ are formed by complete decomposition of 2.5 mol of KClO₃?
questions.ai_explanation: The balanced equation is 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. Two moles of chlorate produce three moles of oxygen, so 2.5 mol produces 2.5×3/2 = 3.75 mol of O₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Balance wH₂SO₄ + xAl(OH)₃ → yH₂O + zAl₂(SO₄)₃ using the smallest whole-number coefficients. What are w, x, y and z?
questions.ai_explanation: One Al₂(SO₄)₃ unit requires two aluminium atoms and three sulfate groups, giving coefficients 2 for Al(OH)₃ and 3 for H₂SO₄. Their 12 hydrogen atoms form 6H₂O. The balanced coefficients are 3, 2, 6 and 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A gas occupies 1.50 dm³ at 25 °C and 1 atm. What volume does the same amount occupy at 100 °C and 1 atm?
questions.ai_explanation: At constant pressure, volume is proportional to absolute temperature. Convert 25 °C and 100 °C to about 298 K and 373 K. Then V₂ = 1.50×373/298 ≈ 1.88 dm³. Celsius temperatures cannot be used directly in the ratio.
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, volume is proportional to absolute temperature. Convert 25 °C and 100 °C to about 298 K and 373 K. Then V₂ = 1.50×373/298 ≈ 1.88 dm³. Celsius temperatures cannot be used directly in the ratio.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 100 cm³ of O₂ passes through a porous plug in 50 s. Under the same conditions, how long does the same volume of H₂ take through that plug? [O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: For equal volumes under the same conditions, diffusion time is proportional to the square root of molar mass. Thus t(H₂) = 50×√(2/32) = 12.5 s. Hydrogen has one-sixteenth the molar mass of oxygen and diffuses four times as fast.
questions.explanation: For equal volumes under the same conditions, diffusion time is proportional to the square root of molar mass. Thus t(H₂) = 50×√(2/32) = 12.5 s. Hydrogen has one-sixteenth the molar mass of oxygen and diffuses four times as fast.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which quantity measures the average kinetic energy of a substance’s molecules?
questions.ai_explanation: Temperature indicates average molecular kinetic energy. In the ideal-gas model, average translational kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature. Volume, mass and pressure are not direct measures of this average energy.
questions.explanation: Temperature indicates average molecular kinetic energy. In the ideal-gas model, average translational kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature. Volume, mass and pressure are not direct measures of this average energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What does the nucleus of tritium, ³H, contain?

options.D: Two neutrons, one proton and one electron

questions.explanation: Tritium is hydrogen-3. Hydrogen has atomic number 1, so its nucleus contains one proton. Mass number 3 means there are two additional nucleons, both neutrons. The electron of a neutral tritium atom is outside its nucleus.

questions.question: In the nuclear equation ¹⁴₇N + X → ¹⁷₈O + ¹₁H, what is X?
questions.ai_explanation: Conservation of mass number gives 14 + A = 17 + 1, so A = 4. Conservation of atomic number gives 7 + Z = 8 + 1, so Z = 2. X is therefore ⁴₂He, an alpha particle or helium nucleus.
questions.explanation: Conservation of mass number gives 14 + A = 17 + 1, so A = 4. Conservation of atomic number gives 7 + Z = 8 + 1, so Z = 2. X is therefore ⁴₂He, an alpha particle or helium nucleus.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which factors can affect the solubility of a gas in a liquid? I. Nature of the solvent; II. Nature of the solute; III. Temperature; IV. Gas pressure.
questions.ai_explanation: Gas solubility depends on how the gas and solvent interact, so both chemical identities matter. Temperature changes dissolution equilibrium, and the gas’s partial pressure also affects how much dissolves. All four listed factors can therefore affect solubility.
questions.explanation: Gas solubility depends on how the gas and solvent interact, so both chemical identities matter. Temperature changes dissolution equilibrium, and the gas’s partial pressure also affects how much dissolves. All four listed factors can therefore affect solubility.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: P, Q, R and S have 1, 2, 3 and 7 outer-shell electrons, respectively. Which is least likely to be a metal?

questions.question: Which listed gas contributes to acid rain through reactions involving atmospheric water?

questions.question: Chlorination of a town water supply primarily controls which of the following?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed substance is an acid salt?
questions.ai_explanation: NaHS is sodium hydrogen sulfide. It results from replacing only one of the two acidic hydrogens of H₂S with sodium, leaving a hydrogen in HS⁻. This makes it an acid salt by composition; that classification does not mean its aqueous solution must have pH below 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What mass of H₂SO₄ is needed in 0.175 dm³ of 6.00 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ solution? [S = 32.06, O = 16.00, H = 1.00]
questions.ai_explanation: The required amount is concentration×volume = 6.00×0.175 = 1.05 mol. H₂SO₄ has molar mass 2(1.00) + 32.06 + 4(16.00) = 98.06 g mol⁻¹. The mass is 1.05×98.06 = 102.963 g, approximately 103.0 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed using carbon electrodes. What are the main products at the anode and cathode, respectively?
questions.ai_explanation: At the cathode, Cu²⁺ gains electrons and deposits as copper. At the carbon anode, water is oxidised and oxygen is evolved. Thus the anode product is oxygen and the cathode product is copper.
questions.explanation: At the cathode, Cu²⁺ gains electrons and deposits as copper. At the carbon anode, water is oxidised and oxygen is evolved. Thus the anode product is oxygen and the cathode product is copper.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What theoretical mass of magnesium is produced by electrolysis of magnesium chloride for 24 h at 500 A, assuming all the current deposits magnesium? [F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹; Mg = 24]
questions.ai_explanation: The charge is 500×24×3600 = 43,200,000 C. Each Mg²⁺ ion needs two electrons, so the magnesium amount is Q/(2F) = 43,200,000/(2×96,500) ≈ 223.8 mol. Its mass is 223.8×24/1000 ≈ 5.4 kg.
questions.explanation: The charge is 500×24×3600 = 43,200,000 C. Each Mg²⁺ ion needs two electrons, so the magnesium amount is Q/(2F) = 43,200,000/(2×96,500) ≈ 223.8 mol. Its mass is 223.8×24/1000 ≈ 5.4 kg.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In MnO₂ + 2Cl⁻ + 4H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O, what are the changes in oxidation number per atom of Mn, Cl and H, respectively?

questions.explanation: Manganese changes from +4 in MnO₂ to +2 in Mn²⁺, a change of −2. Chlorine changes from −1 in Cl⁻ to 0 in Cl₂, a change of +1 per atom. Hydrogen stays at +1, so its change is 0. Reduction means manganese gains electrons.

questions.question: In 2S₂O₃²⁻ + I₂ → S₄O₆²⁻ + 2I⁻, which species is the oxidising agent?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At the same temperature, how are the equilibrium constants for a reaction and its exact reverse related?

options.D: Their product is always greater than 1

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which equilibrium has no net shift when its volume is decreased at constant temperature?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For xP + yQ ⇌ mR + nS, with all species included in the concentration expression, which formula gives Kc?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed combinations are conventional fuel–oxygen pairs used for metal welding? I. Oxygen and ethyne; II. Hydrogen and ethyne; III. Hydrogen and oxygen; IV. Ethyne, hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.ai_explanation: Oxygen with ethyne forms the oxyacetylene flame used in gas welding. Oxygen with hydrogen forms an oxyhydrogen flame that can join suitable lower-melting metals. Hydrogen and ethyne alone are both fuels and do not supply the oxidising gas needed for these conventional torch combinations.
